items.title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
items.summary: Nature Communications, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77107-w Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation.

items.title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
items.summary: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. Its multiscale dynamics, intermittency, extreme events, rough velocity fields and intrinsically stochastic transport make visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectral agreement insufficient measures of physical fidelity. We examine where generative AI provide novel capabilities with emphasis on diffusion models, score-based methods, and related probability-transport formulations. We discuss their use in unconditional generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, temporal evolution, and mesh-free representations. We argue that validation must address turbulence properties: energy transfer, structure functions, anomalous scaling, pdf tails, coherent structures, conservation laws, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity and generalization. Finally, we discuss potential limitations in validation, baseline, data availability and reproducibility, and the need for a benchmark ecosystem combining open data, standardized challenges, hidden tests, physics-aware metrics, and documented failures. This paper serves as a bridge between two communities. For AI practitioners, we provide a fair and accessible introduction to turbulence, essential for appreciating the challenges posed by the field and for assessing the physical relevance of generative models. For turbulent practitioners, we provide an introduction to the key technological aspects of Generative AI, clarifying what these tools actually do, and where their potential and current limitations lie.

items.title: Viscosity variation in fluid flows across scales
items.summary: Although most treatments of fluid mechanics consider the fluid viscosity to be constant or uniform, many systems have a viscosity that varies in time or space. Examples arise in microbial habitats, in the ocean, and in Earth’s mantle. In this review, the authors explain how viscosity gradients occur in real systems, examine how these gradients lead to new phenomena at both low and high Reynolds number, and highlight open research questions.

items.title: Nonlocal Einstein Relation in Confined Phonon Hydrodynamics
items.summary: Einstein relations connect carrier mobility to macroscopic transport coefficients and constitute a fundamental link between microscopic dynamics and transport. In phonon hydrodynamics, this connection is conventionally local: the drift-induced thermal conductivity is proportional to the local drift mobility. Here we show that this relation becomes intrinsically nonlocal under spatial confinement. We derive a nonlocal Einstein relation, $κ_H(y) = \int P(y-y')μ(y'),dy'$, in which hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$ at one position depends on collective drift mobility $μ(y')$ across the entire cross-section of the channel. In the small-Knudsen-number limit, our nonlocal theory recovers the viscous heat equation and the local Einstein relation. At finite Knudsen number, nonlocality produces intrinsic boundary slip and distinct size-scaling behavior of the drift mobility $μ$ and hydrodynamic thermal conductivity $κ_H(y)$. First-principles calculations for graphite show that nonlocality broadens the channel-size window over which thermal conductivity exhibits superlinear size dependence. Temperature-dependent simulations further show that the nonlocal theory captures the emergence of a hydrodynamic peak in thermal conductivity normalized by ballistic conductance, whereas the local theory fails to accurately predict its magnitude. Our results establish a microscopic connection between collective phonon mobility and heat conduction beyond local hydrodynamics.

items.title: Local Search with Correlated Randomness
items.summary: The running-time distribution of a randomized algorithm is computed under independent randomness, but independence is rarely what a source guarantees. We study sources $ν$ satisfying $ν[w]\le DP[w]^s$ for every finite prefix $w$ of the random tape, where $P$ is an independent reference law, $0<s\le1$, and $D\ge1$; individual choices may be predictable, even determined by the past. The worst-case probability of any closed tape event $E$ is exactly $\min\{1,DC_s(E)\}$, where $C_s(E)$ is the infimum cost of covering $E$ by prefixes of varying depth, a tree max-flow/min-cut identity that makes worst-case survival probabilities exact and optimizable over the algorithm's choices. Three applications follow. For $n$ tasks on one machine, each retried until the next random symbol lies in its success set, every schedule has the same makespan distribution under independent randomness, yet under our constraint two fixed orders miss a linear deadline with worst-case probabilities $1$ and $\exp[-Θ(n)]$; a static priority rule is optimal at every deadline. For the standard local walk on a $k$-CNF with an assignment that satisfies a majority of each clause, we determine the sharp source threshold $s_*$. Below $s_*$, on some instances a single admissible source forces nontermination however clauses are selected; at $s_*$, with fixed $D$, the expected number of flips is at most cubic in the initial Hamming distance, against linear under independence, with matching worst-case instances; and any fixed margin above $s_*$ restores linear dependence on the distance. Third, verified backtracking for noisy predecessor search remains correct under a sufficiently strong bound on the comparison errors. In every setting the algorithm may also restart, which supplies no fresh randomness; restarting restores exponential tails exactly when the nontermination event has a prefix cover of cost below one.

items.title: Interaction dependence of the critical correlation length amplitude ratio in anisotropic scalar lattice $φ^4$ theory
items.summary: We investigate critical correlations in the weakly anisotropic two-dimensional scalar lattice $φ^4$ theory and demonstrate that a previously reported independence of the correlation length amplitude ratio from the local interaction strength does not hold. Monte Carlo simulations instead reveal a pronounced dependence of this ratio on the interaction strength. As the coupling is increased, the amplitude ratio interpolates between the continuum and Ising limits, highlighting a nontrivial interplay between lattice effects and local interactions. These findings call for a revised theoretical description of anisotropy effects at finite coupling in this prototypical lattice field theory.

items.title: Effective Hamiltonian description on monitored Majorana chains: correlated power-law hoppings and unconventional entanglement scaling
items.summary: We investigate the structure of effective Hamiltonians governing monitored dynamics of a one-dimensional Majorana chain using Lyapunov spectral analysis. We focus on the gapless phase of the Lyapunov spectrum, where the effective Hamiltonians behave differently from conventional critical Hamiltonians in isolated systems; the spectral gap closes faster than $1/L$ but slower than $1/L^2$ and the entanglement entropy grows as $[\ln(L)]^2$ where $L$ is the system size. We find that the effective Hamiltonians have random long-range power-law hoppings with nontrivial magnitude correlations, rather than being independently and identically distributed. To elucidate the role of these non-Gaussian correlations, we construct random power-law hopping models that capture the essential features of the effective Hamiltonians. The spectral gaps of the constructed models decay faster than $1/L$ but slower than $1/L^2$. We find that, in the absence of hopping correlations, the ground-state entanglement exhibits $\ln(L)$ scaling. In the presence of correlations, by contrast, the entanglement entropy is enhanced and its system-size dependence is consistent with $[\ln(L)]^2$ scaling over the system sizes studied. These results suggest that correlations among long-range hopping magnitudes are responsible for the entanglement scaling rarely encountered in the ground states of conventional isolated quantum systems.

items.title: Implications of an analysis of the shear transformation of a zone of an oblate spheroid for dislocation theory, grain boundary sliding and superplasticity
items.summary: Grain boundary sliding models of superplastic flow take the elementary event to be the shear of an oblate-spheroidal unit embedded in a solid matrix, whose rate follows transition state theory. The mechanics of this unit, and the assumptions linking it to dislocations and macroscopic flow, have not been stated explicitly. Here the unit is analysed as an Eshelby inclusion, a continuum, mathematical treatment without using physical concepts. The analysis gives closed-form shear and volumetric energy coefficients ($0.4456$ and $0.8889$ for aspect ratio $1/2$ and Poisson ratio $1/3$) and shows that the shear stress of the unit is a force dipole, decaying as $r^{-3}$ and changing sign with direction, unlike a dislocation. The inputs, assumptions and proposals needed to connect this unit of shear to dislocation theory and superplastic flow are then stated and classed as experimentally validated, physically realistic or fitting constants. Under three such proposals, a row of about four units acquires the Peierls-Nabarro profile of a full dislocation, and two to three units that of a Shockley partial; the Peierls and Frank-Read stresses and the stacking-fault energy then follow from experimental inputs. With the unit energy as the free energy of activation and strains fitted to superplastic data, the flow law reproduces all 52 measured strain rates of a Cu alloy within an order of magnitude. Molecular-dynamics calculations for Cu outline the extension to dislocation emission, mesoscopic grain boundary sliding and the inverse Hall-Petch effect. This gives phenomenological models of superplastic flow a mechanical basis.

items.title: Coexistence of Ferromagnetic and Overscreened Kondo Effects in a Single Molecule
items.summary: The quest for quantum ground states beyond the Fermi-liquid paradigm remains a central challenge in many-body physics. The ferromagnetic Kondo effect is an intriguing variant of the Kondo effect in which an asymptotically free spin gives rise to singular Fermi-liquid behavior. Despite its theoretical importance, this regime has eluded experimental observation owing to subtle spectroscopic signatures, small energy scales, and symmetry constraints in nanostructures. Here, we demonstrate the coexistence of ferromagnetic and overscreened Kondo effects within a molecular spin system---a triangulene dimer comprising spin-1 and spin-1/2 units adsorbed on a metal surface. Low-temperature scanning tunneling spectroscopy reveals signatures of singular Fermi-liquid behavior, supported by many-body calculations. The molecular design provides control over spin configuration and coupling asymmetry, allowing distinct regimes within the same platform. Our results establish a strategy for realizing non-Fermi-liquid physics at the atomic scale and demonstrate that ferromagnetic Kondo behavior can be deliberately engineered in molecular systems.

items.title: Occupation counts of rarely switching Markov chains: stratified local laws, support selection and the boundary layer
items.summary: A Markov chain with exit rates $q_i$ runs for $N$ steps with transition matrix $I+(T/N)Q$. On each irreducible face that carries start mass, we prove a local limit theorem for the occupation counts with an explicit constant and relative error $O(1/T)$, uniformly for $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$ with $\varepsilon\max_iq_i<1$ and on compact subsets of the open face. Up to $O(1)$, minus the log-probability of counts $n$ with support $F$ is $|F|-1$ times $\log(N/\sqrt T)$ plus $N$ times the Donsker and Varadhan functional of $I+(T/N)Q$ at $n/N$. Every admissible face has an explicit power of $T$ in its largest probability for large $T\le N^{1/3}$, and a constant given by a finite-dimensional variational formula. For $T=τ\log N$ the face of the mode minimizes $τλ_F+|F|-1$ at first order, with $λ_F$ the exit rate. If an admissible face has $Δ\ge1$ more states than another and an exit rate smaller by $δ>0$, we locate every crossing of their largest probabilities for large $T\le N^{1/3}$ up to $O(1/\log N)$. For two irreducible faces the crossing is unique for large $N$ in $1\le T\le\varepsilon N$, with coefficient $1/2$ of $\log\log N$. Near a facet, the continuous-time occupation density is the facet density times an explicit kernel, with relative error $O(1/T)$ at times $x\le cT$ off the facet, $c$ small. The counts obey a lattice form with extra error $T^2/N$ for $T\le\varepsilon_1\sqrt N$. The kernel is Bessel for $x=o(T)$ at facet profiles where the removed state has equal entry and exit laws, and at a profile where the rate has a first correction, of order $m\ge3$, if and only if $x=o(T^{1-2/m})$. On the complete graph with the uniform start, each face of at least 2 states crosses a vertex exactly once.

items.title: Parity-selected charging and noise-correlated work retention in a coupled Si/SiGe double quantum dot battery: theory and experimentally parameterized modeling
items.summary: We investigate extractable work storage in a capacitively coupled double quantum dot (DQD) quantum battery (QB) subjected to experimentally motivated detuning charge noise. The battery is modeled as two interacting charge qubits with an Ising-type capacitive coupling and is charged by resonant microwave modulation of the tunnel coupling channel. Detuning fluctuations are introduced as classical stochastic processes generated from a band-limited 1/f noise spectrum. For each noise realization, the evolution remains unitary, whereas decoherence and loss of contrast emerge after ensemble averaging. We analyze the total ergotropy, its population and coherent contributions, the energy basis populations, a passive ordering violation diagnostic, and the Jensen-Shannon coherence of the noise-averaged state. The results show that resonant tunnel coupling driving selects a dominant E0 <-> E3 population transfer channel in the interacting DQD spectrum. The dominant extractable work is stored in non-passive population distributions, in agreement with recent population ordering interpretations of ergotropy in QBs, while coherence accompanies and supports the resonant transfer as a transient dynamical resource. Detuning noise reduces the energy basis coherence amplitude and also weakens the population transfer pathway responsible for the dominant population ergotropy. This framework provides a noise-aware description of semiconductor QB charging based on extractable work rather than on injected energy alone.

items.title: Rigid Band Shift in Electron-Doped Kagome Metal
items.summary: We study the effects of Sn-site doping on the electronic structure of nonmagnetic kagome metal YV$_6$Sn$_{6-x}$Sb$_x$ by infrared spectroscopy and density-functional theory. The results for samples with $x$ = 0 and 1.4 demonstrate that partial substitution of Sn by Sb acts as a rigid shift of the Fermi level while leaving the band dispersion largely intact. Our findings establish Sn-site substitution in YV$_6$Sn$_6$ as a route to systematically investigate band-filling-dependent electronic properties of nonmagnetic kagome metals.

items.title: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
items.summary: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.

items.title: Real-Space Interference from Quantum Metric
items.summary: Real-space interference of wave packets is governed by their central momentum separation and momentum width, which set the oscillation wavelength and spatial envelope, respectively. Here, we show that in crystalline systems, quantum metric distribution in an isolated band can similarly give rise to real-space interference through the evanescent tails of a localized bound state. The location and width of a quantum metric hot spot in the momentum space set a complex wavevector as one evanescent plane wave component of a bound state. Consequently, with multiple quantum metric hot spots, the density distribution of a bound state or the total density of two spatially overlapped bound states exhibits an interference pattern, where the oscillation period and long-range decay length are determined by the momentum-space separation of the hot spots and the width of the narrowest hot spots, respectively. This quantum-geometric interference is particularly pronounced in (nearly) flat bands, where competing scales from band dispersion are suppressed. Furthermore, we demonstrate that using a Josephson STM the real-space interference can be experimentally observed through the tip-position dependence of the Josephson critical current. Our results reveal a direct correspondence between momentum-space quantum geometry and real-space interference, showing how bound-state profiles encode the momentum-resolved quantum metric.

items.title: Dynamic helimagnetism via charged spin current
items.summary: We present a theoretical and numerical study of classical, localized spins coupled to conduction electrons that carry both charge and spin currents, deriving the effective equations of motion from the s-d exchange Hamiltonian. Applied to a periodically arranged one-dimensional spin chain, these equations yield two current-driven helical phases: a static helix stabilized by a pure spin current alone, and a coherently precessing helix that appears once a small charge-current component is added. For a given helical wavenumber, the precession angular frequency $ω$ and the canting ratio $Δ$ toward the hard axis follow analytically from the equations of motion, while the wavenumber $q_{\rm helix}$ of the precessing helix is selected by a heuristically constructed effective Lagrangian. Direct numerical integration of the same equations of motion reproduces all three observables wherever it yields a coherent helix. The helix chirality is set by a long-range, current-generated Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM)-type coupling rather than an intrinsic DM interaction, so materials without bulk or interfacial DM interactions could also host current-controlled helical order. Because the helical pitch, precession frequency, and canting ratio are all continuously tunable by the current amplitudes, these helices could serve as probes of spin currents.

items.title: Nanoscale mapping of native defects in Td-MoTe2 and their impact on graphene-based van der Waals heterostructures
items.summary: We investigate native defects and their impact on the electronic structure of Td-MoTe2 and graphene/Td-MoTe2 van der Waals heterostructures using scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy. STM reveals a high density of circular, hollow surface defects that we attribute to Te vacancies. STS on pristine MoTe2 shows semimetallic, V-shaped dI/dV spectra with subtle low-energy states. The vacancies suppress the tunnelling conductance below the Fermi level without introducing new sharp defect-related resonances, consistent with a vacancy-induced redistribution of Mo-Te spectral weight rather than the appearance of new electronic states. In the heterostructure, graphene preserves these MoTe2 fingerprints with no noticeable graphene doping or charge transfer. Our results demonstrate that isolated native Te vacancies act as spectroscopically weak perturbations to the low-energy electronic structure of graphene. The graphene overlayer further screens their impact on the electronic structure, making graphene/Td-MoTe2 heterostructures intrinsically tolerant to such interface defects.

items.title: Electronic structure, excitonic optical response, and defect stability of RbTlCl3 from first-principles
items.summary: We present a many-body ab initio study of the electronic structure, optical properties, excitonic effects, and defect stability of RbTlCl3. Density functional theory and many-body methods are used to investigate the properties with and without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). The indirect band gaps obtained using PBE-GGA are 0.94 and 0.95 eV with and without SOC, respectively. Optical spectra are calculated using the independent-particle approximation (IPA), IPA with scissor correction (IQPA), random-phase approximation (RPA) with local-field effects (LFEs), and the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE). The maximum imaginary dielectric function is approximately 7 at 2 eV within IQPA and decreases to 5.7 when LFEs are included. BSE calculations yield a peak value of approximately 10.8 at 1.6 eV, revealing strong excitonic effects. Four prominent bright bound excitons exhibit binding energies of 315-365 meV. The main bright exciton is localized in reciprocal space and delocalized in real space. The spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency is estimated to be 15.4% for a 0.5-micrometer-thick film. The absence of imaginary phonon frequencies and the existence of a thermodynamically stable region indicate dynamical and thermodynamic stability. Chemical-potential analysis identifies the chlorine vacancy as the most stable neutral defect under chlorine-poor conditions and the thallium vacancy under chlorine-rich conditions. These findings establish RbTlCl3 as a promising theoretical candidate for photovoltaic applications and provide insights into excitonic effects in inorganic perovskites.

items.title: Subspace-Protected Topological Phases and Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
items.summary: While tremendous research has revealed that symmetry enriches topological phases of matter, more general principles that protect topological phases have yet to be explored. In this Letter, we elucidate the roles of subspaces in free-fermionic topological phases. A subspace property for Hamiltonians enables us to define new topological invariants. It results in peculiar topological boundary phenomena, i.e., the emergence of an unpaired zero mode or zero-winding skin modes, characterizing subspace-protected topological phases. We establish and demonstrate the bulk-boundary correspondence in subspace-protected topological phases. We further discuss the interplay of the subspace property and internal symmetries. Toward application, we also propose possible platforms possessing the subspace property.

items.title: Ground State Energy of Dilute Fermi Gases in 1D
items.summary: We study the one-dimensional spin-$J$ Fermi gas, interacting through a general repulsive 2-body potential, and prove asymptotics of the ground state energy in the dilute limit. The asymptotic behaviour is given in terms of the ground state energy of a spin chain, which is the Heisenberg antiferromagnet in the case of spin-1/2 fermions. We determine similar asymptotics for the Lieb-Liniger-Heisenberg model, showing that a product trial state used by Girardeau is not optimal.

items.title: Sound waves in a backreaction-affected analogue spacetime: acoustic metric, mass, and correlations in Bose-Einstein condensates
items.summary: Analogue gravity describes sound as a field propagating on an effective spacetime set by the background flow, which is usually treated as given; in reality, however, quantum fluctuations also feed back on the medium that defines this spacetime. This raises the question of whether a condensate modified by this backreaction still defines a spacetime for the quantum field, which has not been established so far. Using a number-conserving expansion of a Bose-Einstein condensate, which keeps the classical background and the quantum fluctuation distinct while retaining their mutual coupling, we show that in the sound-wave and eikonal approximations the first-order phase fluctuation still propagates on an acoustic metric of the backreaction-corrected condensate, but is no longer massless: it obeys a Klein-Gordon equation with a spacetime-dependent mass that is generated by the backreaction sources in the continuity and Euler equations and cannot be absorbed into the metric. Backreaction in a Bose-Einstein condensate is thus a change of the analogue spacetime, supplemented by a mass term that has no geometric counterpart. Solving the coupled condensate-Bogoliubov dynamics for a finite, quasi-one-dimensional gas quenched from a noninteracting state, we find that, while the depletion remains below $2\%$, backreaction enhances the canonically normal-ordered equal-point phase correlation by about $10\%$ in the bulk and up to about $20\%$ near the walls, and that the bulk enhancement survives a finite-resolution imaging model.

items.title: Inverse origami inspired by insect morphogenesis: geometric design of wrinkle structures for curved surface formation
items.summary: Insect exoskeletons abruptly acquire complex three-dimensional forms during metamorphosis from larva to pupa. This transformation occurs through the unfolding of preformed wrinkle structures inside the larval body under internal pressure. Inspired by this process, we investigate an inverse-origami strategy for fabricating curved surfaces. Whereas conventional origami produces three-dimensional objects by folding a flat sheet, this strategy produces curved surfaces by unfolding preformed wrinkle structures. The central design problem is to derive a wrinkle structure from a prescribed target surface. Our key idea is to regard a wrinkle structure as a unidirectional stretching field, which specifies at each point the stretch produced when the structure unfolds. We first derive such a field from the target surface geometry and then translate it into spatially varying wrinkle directions and spacing, so that the wrinkle structure unfolds into the target. The resulting numerical designs approximate the intrinsic metric of the target surface. We demonstrate the method on multiple target surfaces through numerical construction, mechanical unfolding simulations, and 3D-printed prototypes. This work provides a biologically inspired geometric design principle for encoding prescribed surface shapes in wrinkle structures, as well as a framework for designing and fabricating deployable curved surfaces.

items.title: SymADiT: Symmetry-Aware Crystal Generation with Latent Flow Matching
items.summary: Tackling the task of crystal generation, we aim to enhance the previously proposed, symmetry-agnostic, All-atom Diffusion Transformer (ADiT) by introducing SymADiT, a symmetry-aware variant. To do so, we use a representation of crystals based on Wyckoff positions. We follow ADiT and perform generative modelling in latent space, adapted to our symmetry-aware representation. By forcing the output of the generative model to adhere to the symmetry restrictions imposed by the generated crystal's space group and each atom's Wyckoff position, the generated crystals exhibit more realistic symmetry properties. We benchmark our method against both symmetry-aware and symmetry-agnostic models for crystal generation and show competitive performance, generating stable, symmetric, and physically plausible crystals with only an off-the-shelf Transformer architecture. Our code is available at https://github.com/Karmush21/SymADiT.

items.title: Quantum field theory for spin operator of the photon
items.summary: All elementary particles in nature can be classified as fermions with half-integer spin and bosons with integer spin. Within quantum electrodynamics (QED), even though the spin of the Dirac particle is well defined, there exist open questions on the quantized description of spin of the gauge field particle -- the photon. Using quantum field theory, we discover the quantum operators for the spin angular momentum (SAM) $\boldsymbol{S}_{M}=(1/c)\int d^{3}x\boldsymbolπ\times\boldsymbol{A}$ and orbital angular momentum (OAM) $\boldsymbol{L}_{M}=-(1/c)\int d^{3}xπ^μ\boldsymbol{x}\times\boldsymbol{\nabla}A_μ$ of the photon, where $π^μ$ is the conjugate canonical momentum of the gauge field $A^μ$. We also reveal a perfect symmetry between the angular momentum commutation relations for Dirac fields and Maxwell fields. We derive the well-known OAM and SAM of classical electromagnetic fields from the above defined quantum operators. Our work shows that the spin and OAM operators commute which is important for simultaneously observing and separating the SAM and OAM. The correct commutation relations of orbital and spin angular momentum of the photon have applications in quantum optics, topological photonics as well as nanophotonics and can be extended in the future for the spin structure of nucleons.

items.title: Equivalent Pseudo-angular Momentum Governs Selective Magnon-Phonon Hybridization
items.summary: Magnon-phonon hybridization provides a powerful route to couple spin and lattice excitations, yet the symmetry principle governing mode selectivity remains unclear. Here, we show that crystalline pseudoangular momentum provides a general criterion for selective magnon-phonon hybridization in noncollinear multisublattice magnetic systems. The rotation eigenvalue associated with pseudoangular momentum encodes polarization transformations, sublattice permutations, and Bloch phases, requiring magnetoelastic coupling between modes belonging to the same rotation sector. We illustrate this principle in a stacked kagome model with noncollinear spin order. An out-of-plane magnetic field tunes one magnon sector into resonance with a degenerate phonon doublet, yet only the pseudoangular-momentum-matched phonon develops a pronounced avoided crossing while the other remains nearly unmixed. Field reversal switches the selected rotation sector and reverses the rotational polarization of the hybridized phonon component without changing the hybrid-mode energies. Our results reveal pseudoangular-momentum matching as a general framework for understanding and controlling mode-selective spin-lattice hybridization.

items.title: Helicity-Selective Electron-Phonon Coupling Between $PT$-Partner States in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$
items.summary: Rotational symmetry ($C_n$) constrains chiral phonons, but how other symmetries affect their interactions remains largely unexplored. We perform a theoretical and computational study of chiral phonon coupling to parity-time ($PT$)-degenerate electron doublets in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$. Although $PT$ suppresses phonon singlet chirality, chiral phonon doublets can helically interact with $PT$-partner electronic states via a mechanism similar to pseudospin. Selection rules are then analyzed with the interplay of $PT$ and $C_3$. Our computational results of $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$ suggest chiral phonons may be used to resolve intravalley electronic states in $PT$ systems.

items.title: Skin phase transition of a skyrmion in a ferromagnetic superfluid
items.summary: Compared with a scalar Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), a spinor BEC supports richer phenomena because of its internal spin degrees of freedom, including topological solitons such as domain walls or skyrmions. Here, we theoretically reveal three distinct axisymmetric soliton structures formed as a circular domain wall in a spin-1 BEC, connected within fixed winding numbers. We refer to these structures as the broken-axisymmetry (BA)-skin, antiferromagnetic (AF)-skin and normal-core phases. Their occurrence is controlled by the two dimensionless parameters in the absence of linear Zeeman coefficient $p=0$: $q/μ$, the ratio of the quadratic Zeeman coefficient to the chemical potential, and $c_s/c_n$, the ratio of spin interaction to the density interaction. The BA-skin and AF-skin phases exhibit local easy-plane magnetic order and local easy-plane spin-nematic order, respectively, while the normal-core phase is similar to a doubly quantized vortex analogous to that of a scalar BEC with a density depletion at the center. We obtain semi-analytical estimates of selected transition boundaries separating these phases by analyzing the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equation and also numerically confirm them by solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. We estimate the skyrmion radius using a hydrostatic approximation and compare the result with numerical solutions. We envision our results on skyrmions in a spin-1 BEC can trigger further investigation on novel soliton structures in a magnetic superfluid.

items.title: Non-extensive entropy of Vinen quantum turbulence
items.summary: In Ref. [1] the statistical structure of the turbulent cascade in the context of non-additive entropy was considered. Here we suggest that the vortex line ensemble in the Vinen quantum turbulence in superfluids is described by the non-extensive Tsallis-Cirto statistics with $δ=3$. This in particular leads to the temperature, which describes the thermodynamics of the Vinen ensemble, $T\sim mv^2$, where $v$ is the velocity of the flow and $m$ is the mass of the atom of the superfluid liquid.

items.title: Physical Adjoint Learning in Wave Systems with Asymmetric Couplings
items.summary: Developing self-optimizing physical systems that learn directly from their response to external stimuli offers a promising route toward adaptive and intelligent machines. A key ingredient is the ability to evaluate optimization gradients within the physical hardware, bypassing the need for accurate numerical models. In wave systems, \textit{in-situ} adjoint methods provide this capability by exploiting reciprocity to physically realize the adjoint dynamics. However, this approach generally breaks down in nonreciprocal systems, where the adjoint field cannot be directly accessed through the original device. Here, we develop an \textit{in-situ} adjoint optimization framework that extends physical gradient computation to wave systems with asymmetric couplings through computationally low-cost similarity transformations between the forward and transposed operators. We utilize available degrees of freedom like tailored injected excitations, targeted measurements, and tunable parameters, to enable adjoint field reconstruction through forward experiments on the same physical platform. We demonstrate the versatility of the protocol through broadband transmission and isolation, coherent perfect absorption, programmable wavefront shaping, and spatially selective sensing. Our results provide a route to self-optimization in complex nonreciprocal wave systems through efficient physical gradient-based learning. The number of experiments required by the protocol does not increase with the number of optimization parameters, and the method remains applicable even when parts of the system are completely inaccessible.

items.title: Lattice Symmetry Remnants in Spatial and Temporal Entanglement of Quantum Critical Spin Chains
items.summary: Quantum critical lattice models carry universal information beyond the bulk data of their infrared conformal field theory (CFT): microscopic lattice symmetries constrain how the CFT is realized. We probe these remnants through the spatial and temporal entanglement of two Euclidean-evolved states from the same critical model. In the finite-length scaling regime, a conformal boundary encodes the long-distance effect of the short-range initial state, and boundary CFT (BCFT) organizes the universal low-lying entanglement spectrum. We formulate the temporal state as a uniform infinite matrix product state evolved by a symmetry-preserving infinite matrix product operator, using a local factorization regular even at arbitrarily small Trotter steps. For the Ising and three-state Potts chains, whose relevant symmetries are onsite, the spatial and temporal constructions approach the same BCFT structure; varying the initial state engineers conformal boundaries distinguishable spectroscopically. The spin-1/2 XXZ chain instead realizes a Lieb--Schultz--Mattis (LSM) constraint between internal U(1) symmetry and one-site translation. A U(1)-preserving short-range spatial state accommodates it through a doubled unit cell and inequivalent entanglement cuts, whereas the temporal state remains uniform along Euclidean time. Successive spatial transfer steps pump the temporal entanglement spectrum between translation-related Dirichlet sectors, equivalently between integer and half-integer compact-boson zero modes. Breaking U(1) removes both the zero mode and the alternation. Continued evolution at fixed bond dimension crosses over from the finite-length BCFT regime to a finite-entanglement regime generated by symmetry-allowed relevant deformations. Thus microscopic symmetry and anomaly data remain visible in universal entanglement by constraining the boundary realization of the infrared CFT.

items.title: Phonon evidence for a partial, re-entrant spin reorientation near room temperature in LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$
authors: Subha Maity, Dushyant Singh, Vigneshwari S R, Tharundev V V, Navneet Sharma, Subhavenkadesh SS, Krista R. Khiangte
items.summary: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO$3$, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the $a$ axis below $T{\mathrm N}\approx740$~K. Here, we investigate LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$ ($x=0$ and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO$_3$ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace $\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.

items.title: Nonadiabatic vibrational dynamics of CO on Pt(111) studied with first-principles many-body perturbation theory
authors: Ra\'ul Bomb\'in, I\~naki Fern\'andez Tena, J. I\~naki Juaristi, Maite Alducin
items.summary: We investigate the nonequilibrium vibrational dynamics of CO adsorbed on Pt(111), a prototypical adsorbate-surface system for ultrafast vibrational spectroscopy, using a first-principles framework that combines many-body perturbation theory with density functional theory. Within this methodology we explicitly account for electron-hole pair excitations and electron-mediated phonon-phonon coupling. For the latter mechanism, we evaluate the vertex-correction screening, what constitutes a methodological novelty. Our calculations qualitatively reproduce the transient evolution of the internal stretch vibrational mode observed in femtosecond pump-probe experiments, allowing us to identify in the experimental measurements a small transient blueshift after excitation with a femtosecond laser pulse. As predicted in a previous work, the reduction in the number of electronic states available for electron-phonon coupling when the electronic temperature raises at a group 10 transition metal surface, effectively screens the electron-phonon interaction giving rise to an anomalous transient blue-shift.

items.title: Thermoelectric properties and modulation doping of ultrawide-bandgap nitride monolayers
items.summary: Two-dimensional III-nitride alloys provide a composition-tunable platform for exploring thermoelectric transport and intrinsic electric-field tolerance. We combine first-principles electronic-structure calculations with semiclassical transport for ordered monolayer B$_{x}$Al$_{1-x}$N and B$_{x}$Ga$_{1-x}$N. State-dependent momentum relaxation times computed with AMSET include acoustic deformation-potential and piezoelectric scattering. Using a common, temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity of 550 W/mK, we predict maximum thermoelectric figure of merit ZT>2.5 for selected p- and n-type monolayers and ZT>2 at 300~K for n-type B$_{0.25}$Ga$_{0.75}$N. Composition-dependent band curvature, screening, and scattering help interpret the different p- and n-type responses. Vacuum-referenced band alignments identify candidate modulation-doping partners for both carrier types; explicit hGaN/V$_2$O$_5$ calculations yield a hole surface density of approximately 1.6$\times10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$. A separate phenomenological model using the band gap and maximum phonon frequency predicts intrinsic breakdown fields of 20.06 and 20.74 MVcm for the Al- and Ga-containing x=0.75 alloys, respectively. These results motivate further investigation for thermoelectric and high-field power-electronic applications. The ZT values apply to the specified scattering and lattice-conductivity models, while the breakdown estimates require validation for monolayers and do not resolve field direction.

items.title: Low-energy collective electronic excitations in a gold monolayer
authors: Vyacheslav M. Silkin, Maxim Yu. Kagan
items.summary: The low-energy plasmonic properties of a free-standing Au(111) monolayer, frequently referred to as goldene, are investigated by time-dependent density functional theory in the random phase approximation. In the evaluation of dielectric and loss functions the first-principle band structure characterized by a single $s-p$ energy band at the Fermi level is taken into account. In this system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi surface the calculations show the presence, besides the standard two-dimensional (2D) plasmon mode, at even lower energies of three anomalous branches in the momentum-energy region usually assigned to incoherent electron-hole pairs. This is an unexpected result since the electronic system of the gold monolayer is characterized by a single energy band crossing the Fermi level. The dispersion of these anomalous plasmonic branches is strongly anisotropic in-plane and gapless. A general feature is that at small in-plane momentum transfers the modes have a sound-like dispersion in certain momentum directions. We rely the appearance of these anomalous modes to a notable deviation of the Fermi surface of a gold monolayer from a circular shape. As a result of its almost perfect hexagon shape, there is possibility to realize in a {\it single} electronic energy band a scenario of a multi-component electron system with the carrier groups moving with different Fermi velocities in certain momentum directions. The found modes correspond to the out-of-phase charge oscillations of the carriers at different sides of the hexagonal Fermi surface. Hence our work presents evidence how in a metal system with apparently simple band structure around the Fermi level its shape can result in conversion of single-particle charge excitations into collective charge excitations.

items.title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
items.summary: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

items.title: Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
authors: Bahruz Suleymanli, Samir Tariverdiev, B. Tanatar
items.summary: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. In crossed fields, the in-plane electric field generates an effective spin-orbit drift field that modifies the Landau spectrum and spinor states, while at zero magnetic field the problem maps onto Landau--Zener spin dynamics.At zero external fields, the total joint density of states above the band gap remains unchanged, while characteristic subgap structures appear. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. At zero magnetic field, the Franz--Keldysh response shows a crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics as the electric field is reduced. In the weak-field Rashba regime, the field-free singularity becomes a finite peak whose height scales as $\mathcal E^{-1/3}$ and whose position approaches $E_g-E_{\rm SO}$, providing a direct measure of the Rashba energy. In a perpendicular magnetic field, spin-orbit coupling shifts and splits the Landau absorption lines and produces anticrossings without changing their total weights. The Rashba splitting changes from a $\sqrt{B}$ dependence at weak fields to a linear dependence at strong fields. Finally, in crossed electric and magnetic fields, the electric field broadens the Landau lines and drives a continuous crossover toward the Franz--Keldysh regime, while spin-orbit coupling produces opposite shifts and different widths for the two members of each doublet.

items.title: 'Dancing' two-dimensional patterns in nematics above the flexoelectric instability threshold
items.summary: Various types of electrohydrodynamic instabilities in liquid crystals (LCs) are a recurring theme in LC research. The nonlinear stage of the flexoelectric instability in nematics remains the least studied aspect of this phenomenon. This work highlights a key advancement in nonlinear physics, providing a compelling example of nonlinear dynamical system behavior. By solving the system of nonlinear equations for a nematic in an alternating external field, we derive from first principles the unique "dancing" behavior of truly two-dimensional patterns above the flexoelectric instability threshold. Our analysis is restricted to liquid crystals with negative dielectric permittivity and electrical conductivity anisotropies. The resulting solution represents a stable limit cycle near above the Hopf bifurcation, valid within the parameters range where the solutions characteristic exponent is complex. The generalized two-dimensional Ginzburg-Landau-like phenomenological theory of the phenomenon is developed.

items.title: Strontium Titanate Capping Layers as Kinetic Regulators of Redox Phase Transitions in Oxide Heterostructures
authors: Pooya Abdollahi, Woo Jin Kim, Keaghan Knight, Harold Y. Hwang, Ambrose Seo
items.summary: Oxide capping layers are widely used to protect and stabilize thin-film heterostructures, yet their role in governing phase-transition kinetics remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover the kinetic function of few-nanometer-thick SrTiO$_3$ (STO) capping layers in controlling oxidation and reduction processes, using real-time in situ optical spectroscopic ellipsometry. We show that oxygen diffusion through the nanoscale capping layer constitutes the rate-limiting step, giving rise to diffusion-controlled phase transitions in the underlying materials. As a result, both capping-layer thickness and oxygen partial pressure provide effective handles to tune phase transition temperatures. Quantitative analysis yields an activation energy of $E_A$ = 0.64 $\pm$0.06 eV for oxygen diffusion through STO, highlighting its suitability for precise control of redox reactions in diverse material systems. These results establish oxide capping layers as active kinetic regulators of redox-driven phase transitions and offer a general framework for engineering redox dynamics in complex oxide heterostructures.

items.title: Heat current and noise in a point-like junction between normal metal and fractional quantum hall edge state with $\nu = 1/3$
authors: Redouane Zamoum, Houssam Eddine Farhi, Abdellah Touati, Adeline Cr\'epieux
items.summary: In this study, we investigate heat current correlations between two edge states coupled through a constriction in the fractional quantum Hall regime at filling factor $\nu = 1/3$. This configuration allows us to map the system onto an interacting Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid with a local impurity, where the interaction parameter takes the value $\kappa = 1/2$. This specific parameter value enables the application of the refermionization method. By solving the refermionized Hamiltonian, we compute the heat current and evaluate the finite-frequency heat auto- and cross-correlation functions. Our results reveal asymmetric behavior with frequency, corresponding to absorption and emission noise, respectively. Furthermore, we examine several limiting cases, including low- and high-temperature limits as well as strong- and weak-backscattering regimes. In the weak backscattering regime, the Lorenz number approaches $4L_0$ at high voltage, suggesting a rescaling of the Wiedemann-Franz law due to interactions. A detailed study of the heat current fluctuations has made it possible to identify and derive expressions for the dominant contribution in the various regimes of interest, and to reveal the predominance of partition noise.

items.title: Visualization of Single Spin-chain Propagation using Bragg Coherent Diffraction Imaging
authors: Xiaoqian M. Chen, Justin S. Woods, Ulrich Welp, Wai-kwong Kwok, Ralu Divan, David A. Czaplewski, Scott Dhuey, Sujoy Roy, Rajesh V. Chopdekar, Lance E. De Long, Andi Barbour, Claudio Mazzoli, Ian Robinson, J. Todd Hastings
items.summary: Domain wall dynamics and their manipulation in finite-size systems serve as a promising platform for beyond Moore's law applications. Yet, the imaging techniques to track their motion in real-space and time are limited. Here, we use magnetic domain walls formed in permalloy artificial square lattice to demonstrate that single-shot Bragg coherent diffraction imaging (BCDI) is a powerful approach for this purpose. Our BCDI reconstructed images revealed milliseconds time-scale dynamics of the antiphase magnetic domain walls traveling through an antiferromagnetically ordered sample.

items.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
authors: Harlan Heilman, Em Biegler, Sushil Adhikari, Victor Murcia, Tanner Melody, Fred Woodall, Lars Thomsen, Obaid Alqahtani, Brian A. Collins
items.summary: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

items.title: Poly(vinylidene fluoride) under finite electric displacement fields: a removable $\alpha\!\to\!\delta$ reorientation barrier and a persistent first-order $\delta\!\to\!\beta$ conformational change
authors: Shaohui Qiu, Jacob C. Dean, Rajagopalan Thiruvengadathan, Ramanujam Brahmadesam Thoopul Srinivasa Raghava
items.summary: The $\alpha$, $\delta$, and $\beta$ phases of PVDF are interconverted by electrical poling and mechanical drawing, yet the thermodynamics under a controlled electrical boundary condition has not been established from first principles. We evaluate the zero-temperature free energy at fixed electric displacement $D$ from van der Waals density-functional calculations along two constrained coordinates in a common 24-atom cell: a tilt of the gauche C--C bonds that maps antipolar $\alpha$ onto polar $\delta$ (cell change $<1\%$), and a backbone torsion that straightens TG$^+$TG$^-$ chains into all-trans $\beta$ (chain-repeat strain $10.6\%$). As $D$ increases from 0 to $0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$, the lowest homogeneous free energy switches from $\alpha$ to $\delta$ at $D_{c1}=0.046$~C\,m$^{-2}$ and from $\delta$ to $\beta$ at $D_{c2}=0.157$~C\,m$^{-2}$. At $T=0$ with domain-wall energy neglected, a $\delta$ multidomain state lies $14.3$~meV per cell below homogeneous $\alpha$ at every $D$. A $\Gamma$-point harmonic estimate suggests that vibrations reverse this ordering at room temperature. $\delta$ and $\beta$ coexist for $0.11<0.21$~C\,m$^{-2}$ at $E^*=0.69$~GV\,m$^{-1}$, independent of the screening constant. The tilt barrier falls from $0.66$~eV per cell at $D=0$ to $17$~meV at $D=0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$ (below $k_BT$ at $300$~K), while the torsion barrier remains $0.66$~eV at $D_{c2}$ and $0.34$~eV at $D=0.30$~C\,m$^{-2}$, so $\delta\to\beta$ stays first order. Much of the difference traces to the path effective charge ($0.28e$ for the tilt, $0.18e$ for the torsion). Scaling shows the tilt barrier would survive with the torsion charge; the smaller torsion charge accounts for about half the barrier it retains. The landscape accounts for why a field produces $\delta$ and why $\beta$ is reached by drawing, and suggests that raising that charge could let a field alone produce $\beta$.

items.title: Structural characterization of the rutile-GeO2/TiO2 (001) heterointerface
authors: Imteaz Rahaman, Martha R. McCartney, David J. Smith, Kai Fu
items.summary: Rutile-GeO2 (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor for future high-power device applications because of its favorable combination of physical and electrical properties. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840{\deg} C and 925{\deg} C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. Structural analysis of the latter sample revealed a high density of strain-relieving interfacial dislocations, identified primarily as Lomer-type or 60{\deg}-type, that accommodated the ~4% lattice mismatch between the two materials, while chemical analysis showed very limited interfacial intermixing. Crystallographic analysis showed that the interface faceting was associated with rutile {101} facets, with characteristic facet angles of ~114{\deg}; these observations support thermally driven TiO2 (001) substrate faceting rather than an interface reconstruction resulting from GeO2 epitaxy. Overall, these findings provide useful insights into the mechanisms governing interface formation and strain relaxation in r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructures and suggest that further refinement of growth conditions should enable improved epitaxial growth of r-GeO2 for future ultrawide-bandgap electronic device applications.

items.title: Dipole chains of Bloch point singularities revealed by X-ray magnetic tomography
authors: Jeffrey Neethirajan, Rikako Yamamoto, Marisel Di Pietro Mart\'inez, Luke A. Turnbull, Praveen Vir, Chandra Shekar, Claudia Felser, Luis Carlos Colocho Hurtarte, Benedikt J. Daurer, Majid Kazemian, Burkhard Kaulich, Claire Donnelly
items.summary: Bloch point singularities play an important role in magnetic systems, mediating changes in topology in three dimensional configurations. However, until now they have only been observed as isolated objects or as part of individual topological textures. Here we present the experimental observation of a 1D dipole chain of Bloch points in an anisotropic chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic vector tomography. We identify that the chain of Bloch point singularities lies along a boundary between regions of opposite chirality and that neighbouring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable at separations down to 60 nm. The stability of the Bloch points is determined to be closely related to the surrounding topology of the magnetisation configuration and a threshold separation for the spontaneous annihilation of Bloch point-anti-Bloch point pairs within chiral domain walls is identified to be approximately 90 nm in distance. This observation of a chain of Bloch points and the insight into their stability, offers a route to explore the correlative behaviour of such topological point defects. The behaviour and control of such point defects is of relevance for the control of 3D magnetisation configurations, and provides a new route towards the creation of correlated configurations of singularities in a magnetic system.

items.title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic \texorpdfstring{$\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$}{beta-Ga2O3}
authors: Kai Xu, Shuo Zhao, Luca Sung-Min Choi, Nils Bernhardt, Pouria Emtenani, Felix Nippert, Moritz Mei{\ss}ner, Hans Tornatzky, Oliver Bierwagen, Piero Mazzolini, Riccardo Mincigrucci, Laura Foglia, Danny Fainozzi, Filippo Bencivenga, Zbigniew Galazka, George Fytas, Bartlomiej Graczykowski, Riccardo Rurali, Matthias Scheffler, Christian Carbogno, Juan Sebastian Reparaz, Markus R. Wagner
items.summary: Monoclinic $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. Frequency-resolved ab initio Green--Kubo calculations show that the bulk anisotropy pattern emerges only when the accumulated conductivity includes phonon modes above 4 THz, whereas the sub 3 THz acoustic contributions are nearly isotropic. Extreme-ultraviolet transient thermal grating spectroscopy reveals that reducing the grating period to 28 nm strongly enhances the in-plane thermal anisotropy, most markedly in the (001) plane, where it reaches nearly twice its macroscopic value. Reconstructed and calculated mean-free-path (MFP) accumulation functions link this enhancement to the stronger directional contrast of short-MFP phonons. Together, these results identify high-frequency, short-MFP phonons as the dominant origin of thermal anisotropy in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$, while low-frequency phonons attenuate the directional contrast at macroscopic scales.

items.title: Spatiotemporally-resolved differential dynamic microscopy reveals strain-induced deformations in heterogeneous soft materials
authors: Aysan Razzaghi, Mehrzad Sasanpour, Jasmine Ren, Caidric Gupit, Matthew E. Helgeson, Megan T. Valentine, Rae M. Robertson-Anderson, Ryan McGorty
items.summary: Understanding the microscopic behavior of materials in response to mechanical perturbations is a central challenge in soft matter, yet existing methods, which typically rely on microscopy-based imaging, often struggle with spatial heterogeneity and low signal-to-noise that are characteristic of many soft and biological materials. Additionally, many existing rheo-optical methods focus on the response to macro-scale forces rather than localized perturbations despite the importance of local stresses in biological and industrial applications of soft materials. Here, we present STroboscopically Averaged, time-Resolved Differential Dynamic Microscopy (starDDM) to investigate a sample's deformation across time and distance due to a cyclically applied local force. As proof-of-principle, we use this model-independent and tracer-free approach to map the motions of active cytoskeleton composites imposed by the movement of an optically trapped probe particle embedded within the complex network. We reveal how motor-driven restructuring and varying strain rates tune the magnitude and propagation of the response, which we further show decays with distance from the perturbation. This analytical platform fills a critical gap in micro-rheology, offering a versatile tool for probing the non-equilibrium dynamics of soft materials ranging from biopolymer networks to 3D-printed materials and soft robotics.

items.title: Boundary shape controls the stress distribution in two-component elastic materials
authors: Kyungeun Kim, Adam Clare, Miranda Holmes-Cerfon
items.summary: We investigate how the shape and arrangement of high-stiffness regions govern stress redistribution in two-component triangular elastic spring networks subjected to spatially correlated and uncorrelated random prestress. We compare boundary roughness, partitioning into disconnected regions, and graded transitions between regions of different stiffness. Our simulations identify interface bonds as channels for energy transfer: increasing their number provides additional transfer paths and reduces stress concentration in mechanically rigid regimes, while offering little benefit in compliant subnetworks. This is analogous to defects in naturally occurring crystal structures, where the defects themselves isolate stress. At a fixed fraction of high-stiffness material, partitioning reduces stress concentration for both correlated and uncorrelated prestress. The benefit diminishes with further subdivision as the number of interface bonds becomes comparable to the number of interior nodes. Stress reduction, however, depends on the spatial correlations of the imposed prestress: random prestress generally yields a stronger effect, though the difference diminishes in some regimes. Graded interfaces further reduce peak stress by distributing the stiffness transition over a broader region. Together, these results suggest design strategies based on increasing interface area, matching subdivision scale to prestress correlations, and grading stiffness transitions. This minimal framework identifies how internal structure controls energy transfer and stress redistribution, suggesting design principles for mechanical robustness under both internal and external loading.

items.title: The Extended Diode Equation
authors: Jianhong Yang, Gonghao Sun, Tinglan Li
items.summary: For more than 75 years, the p-n junction current-voltage characteristic has been derived by treating majority carriers as an inert background and conflating the junction voltage with the applied bias. Here we show that the base electric field, generated by the coupling of excess majority and minority carriers, fundamentally alters the internal potential distribution. This self-consistent framework yields a closed-form extended diode equation that reproduces the high-injection roll-off without invoking an external series resistance, thereby eliminating an empirical patch that has persisted in the classical theory.

items.title: Heterogeneous superconductivity emerging from a charge-stripe state in kagome lattices
authors: Hongyu Li, Shuikang Yu, Huachen Rao, Zhuying Wang, Xingchen Zhou, Houpu Li, Yunmei Zhang, Zhao Gong, Xin Yu, Rui Wu, Tao Wu, Zhenyu Wang, Ziji Xiang, Xianhui Chen
items.summary: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. However, recent achievements establish that the interplay between these two collective electronic phenomena can be more perplexing, with emergent phenomena arising from their cooperation. Here we report a distinctive case of the kagome superconductors CsV3Sb5-xSnx, in which the characteristics of superconductivity evolve in accordance with the form of CDW order. As the triple-Q CDW in CsV3Sb5 transforms to a short-range stripelike CDW at xc = 0.07, a sudden change in superconducting properties occurs concomitantly. A combination of thermodynamic, electrical transport and scanning tunneling microscopy experiments reveals a heterogeneous superconducting state beyond xc: the superconducting gap exhibits pronounced spatial variation, in conformity with a distribution of critical temperature and the resulted superconducting precursor effects. Moreover, abundant normal fluid persists deep into the superconducting state, as evidenced by remnants of electronic specific heat and zero-energy quasiparticle interference. These observations are unrelated to the chemical inhomogeneity and residual strain effect introduced by Sn substitution. Instead, they emulate the phenomenology that a sign-changing superconducting order parameter is subject to strong pair-breaking scattering with the short-range charge stripes and hence reflect the unconventional nature of superconductivity developing inside the charge-stripe state.

items.title: A Self-Consistent Two-Carrier Drift-Diffusion Framework for p-n Junctions: Extended Diode Equation, Power Dissipation, and Base Transit Time
authors: Jianhong Yang, Tinglan Li, Gonghao Sun
items.summary: The classical theory of p-n junctions derives the current-voltage characteristic from minority-carrier diffusion alone: majority carriers are treated as an inert background, the quasi-neutral base as field-free, and the junction voltage as equal to the applied bias. These premises fail together under high bias and high-level injection, where the observed current roll-off is reproduced only by appending an empirical series resistance outside the junction physics. Here we develop a self-consistent two-carrier drift-diffusion framework that introduces no assumption beyond the classical ones. Excess majority carriers are shown to be electrostatically forced transport participants: the ambipolar diffusion equation, closed by exact two-sided boundary conditions, yields a unified excess-carrier profile. The resulting base field separates into an ohmic and a Dember component, and all four current components follow in closed form, their sum being position independent. At device level the framework closes into an extended diode equation that contains the Shockley equation as its low-injection, long-base limit and reproduces the n=2 roll-off intrinsically. The junction voltage emerges as a self-limiting drop confined to the space-charge region and separated from the applied bias by exact base drops. Two device-level corrections are quantified: at high current, 75-90% of the dissipation migrates from the junction into the quasi-neutral base, and field-assisted acceleration shortens the base transit time by up to a factor of six. Three parameter-free predictions follow: a universal ideality-factor crossover that passes through 3/2 when the boundary excess equals the doping, a high-injection onset voltage that scales as 119 mV per decade of doping, and a geometry factor that survives into high injection.

items.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
authors: A. A. Shchepkin, D. V. Karlovets
items.summary: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. GaAs is less favorable within the present model because of its larger effective mass and deeper donor levels. We also discuss the demanding photon-wave packet parameters, possible extensions to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and post-emission OAM selection. Although the generation of vortex electrons with a vanishing OAM uncertainty via photoemission seems challenging, we argue that it is still possible to generate single-electron vortex states with a finite OAM dispersion.

items.title: Kinetic competition controls loss-induced exceptional points of Hubbard pairs
items.summary: Two-body loss can bind two fermions in a Hubbard lattice, yet the binding threshold in the infinite lattice need not be an exceptional point (EP). At fixed total momentum $\mathbf{K}$, the hops of the two particles interfere into a relative-motion hopping along each lattice direction, which sets the kinetic energy of the relative motion. On a hypercubic lattice, the threshold $g_c=1/[\pi\rho_2(0)]$ is an EP precisely when the maximum kinetic energy along one direction exceeds the sum of the transverse maxima. This dominance keeps every transverse-momentum scattering channel propagating near the band center, making the local pair Green function purely imaginary there. Two real-energy scattering zeros associated with coherent perfect absorption then coalesce at the threshold into a second-order EP of the analytically continued pair problem, where loss restores the parity-time symmetry of the pair's scattering solutions. Without a dominant direction, binding occurs without coalescence and without breaking of that symmetry. Total momentum can therefore select EP sectors even on isotropic lattices. More broadly, the kinetic structure of the two-particle continuum determines whether loss-induced binding and exceptional degeneracy coincide.

items.title: Zeeman Shift and Injection Currents under Light Irradiation
authors: Ruizhi Dong, Yihua Xiao, Pengfei Wang, Ruixiang Fei
items.summary: The conversion of light into electrical currents enables energy harvesting and photodetection. Conventional second-order dc photocurrents are driven by the electric component of light through electric-dipole coupling and require broken inversion symmetry. Here, we show that the electric and magnetic components of light jointly generate Zeeman shift and injection currents. Using quantum perturbation theory, we derive explicit microscopic expressions for their conductivity tensors. We systematically classify the symmetry constraints on these responses and show how they differ from those governing conventional photocurrents. In particular, both responses can occur in centrosymmetric systems with spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order, irrespective of time-reversal symmetry. A centrosymmetric kagome model exhibits broadband responses. First-principles calculations for Mn$_3$Sn further predict Zeeman injection and shift current densities of $10^{2}$-$10^{3}~\mathrm{A/m^{2}}$ and $1$-$10~\mathrm{A/m^{2}}$, respectively, under illumination with an electric-field amplitude $E=10^{4}~\mathrm{V/m}$. These magnitudes place both currents within experimental reach.

items.title: Compass Correlations in a Square-Lattice Magnet
authors: Otkur Omar, Matthias D. Frontzek, Gabriele Sala, Junying Shen, Xinmin Wang, Ze Hu, Zhuang Xu, Zecong Qin, Xin Tong, Joe Paddison, Max Hirschberger, Shinichiro Seki, Masaaki Matsuda, Matthew B. Stone, Andrew D. Christianson, Nguyen D. Khanh, Shang Gao
items.summary: The square-lattice compass model is a paradigm of bond-dependent frustration, yet experimental evidence for its characteristic spin correlations has remained elusive. Here we identify compass correlations in the square-lattice intermetallic ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ using single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering. Comparative measurements on the isostructural compounds NdRu$_2$Si$_2$ and ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ reveal a pronounced contrast between nearly uniform diffuse rings in the former and strong intensity modulation between Brillouin zones in the latter. Through the magnetic neutron polarization factor, this modulation reveals compass correlations that couple moment orientation to the correlation wavevector. Crystal-field spectroscopy identifies four preferred in-plane orientations for the Er$^{3+}$ moments. A minimal compass-Heisenberg model incorporating this anisotropy quantitatively reproduces the diffuse scattering and accounts for the double-$Q$ vortex-antivortex ground state. Fits with the compass couplings fixed at values set by the dipolar energy scale retain good agreement with the data, supporting a substantial dipolar contribution to the bond-dependent interactions. Our results establish a square-lattice platform for compass physics and suggest that dipolar interactions, acting together with local crystal-field anisotropy, can shape directional magnetic correlations alongside conduction-electron-mediated exchange.

items.title: Magnonic time crystal with lasing coherence
authors: Jiantao Song, C. K. Wei, Shuhuan Ma, Yiming Pan, Zhijian Chen, Li Yu, Wei Lu, Bimu Yao
items.summary: Discrete time crystals (DTC) can respond at an integer multiple of the drive period. Internal order-parameter measurements have advanced studies of this novel non-equilibrium phase of matter; however, turning this order into highly coherent, externally accessible radiation remains challenging: pump-driven nonlinear processes must supply sufficient gain to compensate dissipation while preserving subharmonic stability. Here we realize a room-temperature magnonic time crystal (MTC) with radiation of lasing coherence using a pump-induced magnon mode in yttrium iron garnet. A microwave beat drive produces robust period doubling over a finite parameter range, with spectral signatures of higher-order MTC at stronger driving. The emitted field exhibits linewidth narrowing to 260.0 Hz and a first-order correlation decay time of $995 \mu s$. Our model links this response to three-magnon confluence, yields a stability region consistent with experiment and predicts a possible transition to chaos. We further map the complex temporal dynamics into frequency-resolved nonlinear features for reservoir computing. These results bridge time-crystalline order and nonlinear information processing through intrinsic magnon-magnon interactions and lasing coherence.

items.title: Intrinsic Paramagnetism of Optical Phonons and Thermal Hall Effect in Quantum Paraelectrics
authors: Harsh Jain, Manideep Gone, Nabyendu Das
items.summary: We propose a microscopic theory of the phonon-mediated thermal Hall effect in quantum paraelectrics, driven by the intrinsic paramagnetism due to quantum fluctuations of the (nearly) critical optical phonon modes.
