Here, we show that hierarchical-modular networks naturally generate heterogeneous modular dynamics and firing rates, extending regimes of critical-like dynamics with enhanced intrinsic timescales, reflecting critical slowing down, and diverse scaling exponents without fine-tuning near criticality. Intrinsic timescales increase across hierarchical levels, while their dispersion within levels emerges only when connectivity profiles and firing rates are heterogeneous. We introduce modular dynamic range to quantify how individual modules respond to external inputs and show that heterogeneity enhances both global and module-specific sensitivity, with modular intrinsic timescales increasing with dynamic range. Local stimulation reduces dynamic range in homogeneous networks but enhances it in heterogeneous networks relative to global stimulation. Moreover, selectively stimulating intermediate hierarchical levels maximizes both global and modular dynamic range, revealing a principle of functional specialization. In heterogeneous networks, modular dynamic range is more variable and increases even in unstimulated modules, demonstrating distributed computational benefits beyond directly stimulated regions. Together, these findings establish heterogeneity as a mechanism through which hierarchical-modular networks sustain critical-like dynamics, generate hierarchical timescales, and distribute computational sensitivity, providing a basis for functional specialization without fine-tuning to criticality.

items.title: Multi-scale patterns arising from competing chemotactic interactions
authors: Agniva Datta, Robert Gro{\ss}mann, Carsten Beta
items.summary: Classical chemotaxis models consider the directed motion of cells in response to a chemical gradient. Recent experiments suggest that biological microswimmers such as bacteria can perform chemotaxis toward multiple chemicals, which dynamically evolve depending on the distribution of the microswimmers. In this Letter, we consider a mass-conserving chemotaxis model in which pattern formation is driven by two competing chemicals, autoinducers and nutrients, where the former acts as an activator and the latter as an inhibitor for coarsening. We show that this can give rise to diverse patterns including long wavelength uninterrupted coarsening, Turing-like arrested coarsening, traveling waves as well as a novel class of mixed multi-scale oscillatory coarsening patterns, where a dense aggregate coexist with a dynamically spreading part of the population. We analytically derive the conditions for the onset of such patterns and discuss their physical implications, which significantly broadens our understanding of signaling active matter and pattern formation in general.

items.title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
authors: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham
items.summary: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.

items.title: Entanglement Asymmetry and Asymmetry Contour under Boundary Symmetry Breaking
items.summary: We investigate how symmetry-breaking boundary magnetic fields affect magnetization and R\'enyi-2 entanglement asymmetry (EA) in the transverse-field Ising model. For the ground state, magnetization exhibits qualitatively distinct behaviors in the ordered and disordered phases. EA also exhibits phase-dependent behavior, which is well captured by the lower and upper bounds derived in this work. In the critical regime, both magnetization and EA exhibit behavior qualitatively consistent with the field-theoretical predictions for a related setup. We also study boundary-quench dynamics and find that magnetization propagates from the boundary into the bulk with a velocity consistent with the maximum quasiparticle velocity. In contrast, because EA is a subsystem-integrated quantity, its spatial structure is not directly resolved. We therefore introduce the asymmetry contour, a contour-like finite-difference quantity that provides a spatially resolved characterization of the symmetry-breaking information encoded in the reduced density matrix. The resulting contour is complementary to the local magnetization, retaining sensitivity to nonlocal many-body correlations while its dynamics also reflects the underlying quasiparticle propagation. These results show how EA and its contour can provide complementary information-theoretic characterizations of symmetry breaking and its spatial structure.

items.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning
authors: Yatin Dandi, Matteo Vilucchio, Hugo Tabanelli, Florent Krzakala
items.summary: During joint training, backpropagation allows later layers to reshape earlier representations, a feedback mechanism absent from purely layer-wise learning. We extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a recently proposed layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture this interaction. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we derive a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its corresponding next-layer column. In a controlled small-initialization regime with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, these dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each growing mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper-layer response through shared neuron coefficients. This motivates a backward-coupling algorithm in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps, while corrected features refine upward transmission. A function-space variational principle characterizes the selected feature-response pairs by maximizing the label correlation of their product under kernel-norm constraints. For three-layer networks, we derive self-consistent continuous-time dynamics for the filtered hidden-layer features, the activation kernels, and the network output under the proposed backward coupling. In a hierarchical multi-index model, we establish a feature-recovery separation: backward coupling recovers lower-layer directions invisible to the original forward label-weighted statistic. The linear specialization recovers residual-dependent singular-mode dynamics, while paired modes provide a dynamical mechanism for linked low-rank covariance components consistent with the rainbow-network picture. Experiments with fully connected and convolutional networks on binary CIFAR-10 show improved accuracy over forward Neural LoFi at matched widths.

items.title: Non-singlets and the phase diagram of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
authors: Igor R. Klebanov, Henry W. Lin, Pavel Meshcheriakov, Jessica Yeh
items.summary: The quantum mechanics of one $N\times N$ Hermitian matrix in the infinite $N$ limit is well known to define a two-dimensional string theory when the quartic coupling constant $g$ is tuned to a special negative value $g_*$. We study the thermodynamics of this Matrix Quantum Mechanics (MQM), treating the SU$(N)$ symmetry as a global symmetry. Crucially, the non-singlets, i.e. states in non-trivial representations of SU$(N)$, implement the effects of vortices on the discretized worldsheets. This random lattice model has the low-temperature $c=1$ and high-temperature $c=0$ phases, with the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition separating them. We map out the phase diagram in the coupling--temperature plane, which is separated by the critical stability curve $T_c(g)$ extending from $g_*< g <0$. We study this curve using the non-perturbative matrix bootstrap and low- and high-temperature perturbation theory, which explain the thermal instability. At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we map out the BKT transition in this model.

items.title: SO(5) multicriticality in two-dimensional quantum magnets
authors: Jun Takahashi, Hui Shao, Bowen Zhao, Wenan Guo, Anders W. Sandvik
items.summary: We resolve the nature of the quantum phase transition between antiferromagnetic and valence-bond solid ground states in square-lattice spin-1/2 magnets - the putative deconfined quantum-critical point. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations of J-Q models, in which Heisenberg exchange J competes with multi-spin interactions Qn formed by n singlet projectors, we demonstrate first-order discontinuities increasing with n. For n=2 and n=3, the first-order signatures are very weak and we extract universal scaling dimensions of a proximate multicritical point. Their values coincide closely with known bounds for an SO(5) symmetric conformal field theory (CFT) containing a relevant SO(5) singlet operator that destabilizes the generic deconfined critical point. We characterize the emergent SO(5) symmetry by its scaling dimensions of the leading irrelevant perturbations. Using the J-Q2-Q6 model, we tune the transition from weak to stronger first-order and find scaling of the coexisting order parameters with a large exponent beta ~ 0.85, in agreement with the relevant scaling dimensions of the multicritical point. The exponent that had previously been identified with the correlation length does not have a corresponding CFT level, and we explain it as pseudo-critical length scale of bubbles of one phase inside the other that are compressed in size by an SO(5)-violating irrelevant repulsive interaction between the two order parameters. The bubble scale reflects a hierarchy of excitation gaps generated by the SO(5) perturbation in the neighborhood of the first-order transition, akin to a Higgs mechanism. We argue that the multicritical point is the tip of a gapless spin liquid phase in frustrated Heisenberg models into which the J-Q models can be deformed, but the spin liquid, and perhaps the multicritical point itself, exist outside the regime amenable to sign-free simulations.

items.title: Kagome goldene with flat bands and Dirac nodal line fermions via line-graph epitaxy
authors: Qiwei Tian, Sahar Izadi Vishkayi, Chen Zhang, Jiang Zeng, Bo Li, Li Zhang, Long-Jing Yin, Yuan Tian, Meysam Bagheri Tagani, Lijie Zhang, Zhihui Qin
items.summary: The kagome lattice has emerged as a promising platform for investigating exotic quantum phases. However, achieving a single-atomic-layer kagome lattice in elemental materials remains a significant challenge. Here, we introduce line-graph epitaxy, a novel approach that enables the atomic-scale synthesis of goldene, a monolayer of elemental gold atoms arranged in a kagome lattice. Through scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate the formation of kagome goldene, featuring a flat band with a van Hove singularity approximately 1.1 eV below the Fermi level, signaling strong electron correlation effects. Notably, the flat band is disrupted at the zigzag edges of goldene nanoflakes, revealing substantial edge effects. Furthermore, our calculations show that weak interlayer interactions between goldene and the underlying Au2Ge substrate generate dual Dirac nodal lines through a proximity effect. These findings offer not only a novel strategy for constructing elemental kagome lattices, but also a generalizable framework for fabricating and controlling line-graph materials. This research advances the exploration of quantum phases driven by strong correlations and the design of materials for next-generation quantum technologies.

items.title: Identification and mitigation of errors in hole spin qubit readout
authors: Eoin Gerard Kelly, Leonardo Massai, Bence Het\'enyi, Marta Pita-Vidal, Alexei Orekhov, Cornelius Carlsson, Inga Seidler, Konstantinos Tsoukalas, Lisa Sommer, Michele Aldeghi, Stephen W. Bedell, Stephan Paredes, Felix J. Schupp, Matthias Mergenthaler, Andreas Fuhrer, Gian Salis, Patrick Harvey-Collard
items.summary: High-fidelity readout of spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots can be achieved by combining a radiofrequency charge sensor with spin-to-charge conversion and Pauli spin blockade. However, reaching high readout fidelities with hole spin qubits remains challenging due to site-dependent spin anisotropies and short relaxation times during readout. Here, we analyze the multiple error processes that arise during readout using a double-latched scheme in a germanium double quantum dot hole spin qubit system. We first investigate the spin-to-charge conversion process as a function of magnetic field orientation, and configure the system to adiabatically map the $\lvert \downarrow\downarrow \rangle$ state to the only non-blockaded state. We reveal a strong magnetic field strength dependence of the spin relaxation rates, and minimize it by operating at low fields. We further characterize and mitigate the error processes that arise during the double-latching process. By combining a radiofrequency charge sensor, a double-latching process, and optimized magnetic field parameters, we achieve a single-shot single-qubit state-preparation-and-measurement fidelity of 97.0% while maintaining control of both spins under the readout conditions.

items.title: Intrinsic defects and 4d/5d transition metal defects in Cr$_2$O$_3$: pathways for enhancing the N\'eel temperature
items.summary: First-principles calculations are employed to explore avenues to increase the N\'eel temperature ($T_{\mathrm{N}}$) of the magnetoelectric antiferromagnet Cr$_2$O$_3$ through doping. Employing the hybrid functional method, we calculate the formation energy of intrinsic defects and transition metal dopants (Mo, W, Nb, Ta, Zr, and Hf) to assess their likelihood of formation. Intrinsic defect calculations indicate that Cr interstitials and oxygen vacancies dominate under Cr-rich conditions, whereas Cr vacancies prevail under O-rich conditions. Notably, under Cr-rich conditions, the Fermi level can be pinned slightly above mid-gap due to the formation of Cr interstitials and oxygen vacancies. Additionally, we identify a split Cr vacancy configuration that is more energetically stable than a normal Cr vacancy in corundum Cr$_2$O$_3$. To assess the influence of dopants on $T_{\mathrm{N}}$ of Cr$_2$O$_3$, we calculate the enhancement of the exchange energy for the spin at the dopant site or at an adjacent Cr site using the supercell method.Our study identifies isovalent Mo and W substitutions at Cr sites as the most promising candidates for increasing the N\'eel temperature because of impurity-mediated enhancement of the exchange interaction for half-filled bands. Formation-energy calculations indicate that Mo and W substitutions at Cr sites form more readily under Cr-rich conditions and that a Fermi level near or slightly above midgap stabilizes the desirable neutral charge states of the Mo and W defects. This is assisted by the formation of intrinsic Cr interstitials and O vacancies under Cr-rich conditions. These findings offer a route to utilize defects for higher $T_{\mathrm{N}}$and enhanced performance of Cr$_2$O$_3$ in magnetoelectric devices and provide useful guidance for future experimental studies.

items.title: Resonant dielectric amplification of superconductivity at the FeSe:SrTiOT$_3$ interface
authors: Krzysztof Kempa, Michael J. Naughton, Hanno H. Weitering
items.summary: Epitaxial monolayers of FeSe grown on SrTiO$_3$ (STO) and related polar substrates exhibit superconducting transition temperatures of 65-70 K, far above the ~8 K value of bulk FeSe. Although coupling to interfacial Fuchs-Kliewer (FK) phonons is widely believed to contribute to this enhancement, the apparent universality of high=T$_c$ superconductivity across polar interfaces presents a striking puzzle. Here, we identify the lower-energy FK mode near 59 meV, associated with the bulk longitudinal optical resonance of STO, as a conduit through which the substrate dielectric response enhances pairing in FeSe. Within a phenomenological Migdal-Eliashberg framework, incorporating the measured dielectric response of STO selectively amplifies the pairing interaction near this resonance and raises the theoretical upper bound of T$_c$ into the experimentally observed range. A similar enhancement is reproduced for FeSe on BaTiO$_3$, while related polar substrates such as TiO$_2$, LaFeO$_3$, and EuTiO3 possess the same key electrodynamic ingredients. We refer to this effect as resonant anti-shielding (RAS). More broadly, RAS identifies the bulk electrodynamic response of the substrate as a pairing amplifier, opening a route toward designing superconducting heterostructures through control of their dielectric environment.

items.title: Laser Melting and Loss of Interlayer Coherence of the Charge Density Wave Order in TiSe${_2}$ observed by time-resolved neutron diffraction
authors: K. Dharmasiri (Department of Physics, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, United States), S. S. Philip (Department of Physics, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, United States), D. Louca (Department of Physics, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, United States), S. A. Chen (Neutron Scattering Division, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, United States), M. D. Frontzek (Neutron Scattering Division, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, United States), Z. J. Morgan (Neutron Scattering Division, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, United States), C. Hua (Materials Science and Technology Division, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, United States)
items.summary: Time-resolved elastic neutron scattering combined with laser-induced heating was used to probe the evolution of the periodic lattice distortion (PLD) associated with charge-density-wave (CDW) order in 1T-TiSe$_{2}$. Upon pulsed laser heating, the crystal undergoes a phase transition, where the transient response of the average lattice is isotropic. In contrast, the PLD exhibits an anisotropic behavior. The superlattice intensity is rapidly suppressed in-plane and out-of-plane upon heating, consistent with melting of the ordered state, but recovers more quickly in-plane than along the c-axis as the sample cools below the CDW transition temperature. The out-of-plane component shows pronounced broadening due to reduction of the interlayer correlation length while the in-plane correlations recover. The disparity between the nearly isotropic lattice response and the anisotropic recovery of the superlattice demonstrates that the CDW dynamics cannot be described solely by the evolution of the average lattice temperature. Instead, the results indicate that interlayer phase coherence represents the slowest-relaxing component of the ordered state. These findings support a picture in which the CDW instability is established primarily within the 1T-TiSe${_2}$ layers, while three-dimensional long-range order depends on weaker coupling between layers. More broadly, they demonstrate how direction-resolved time-resolved neutron diffraction can disentangle thermal and correlation-driven contributions to CDW dynamics in low-dimensional materials.

items.title: AI-Guided Computational Design of a Room-Temperature, Ambient- Pressure Superconductor Candidate: Grokene
authors: DEARDAO DeSci Collaborative Team, Yanhuai Ding
items.summary: We introduce Grokene, a novel two-dimensional superlattice derived from graphene, which was identified through an AI-guided materials discovery workflow utilizing a large language model. Grokene is predicted to exhibit ambient-pressure, room-temperature superconductivity, with computational simulations revealing a high electron-phonon coupling constant and a substantial logarithmic-averaged phonon frequency (~1650 K), leading to a mean-field critical temperature of approximately 325 K. Full isotropic Eliashberg solutions further support a critical temperature around 310 K, underscoring its strong potential for room-temperature superconductivity. However, the strict two-dimensional nature of Grokene introduces phase fluctuations, limiting the observable superconducting transition to a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) temperature of about 120 K in monolayers. To elevate TBKT toward room temperature, strategies such as few-layer stacking, substrate or gate engineering, and optimization of superlattice structure and doping levels are proposed. Our integrated workflow, combining AI-driven materials discovery with advanced many-body theories (DFPT/EPW, Eliashberg, and RPA), provides a systematic and reproducible framework for exploring novel superconductors. We suggest that experimental synthesis and comprehensive characterization of Grokene will be essential to assess these computational predictions and to explore routes toward practical superconductivity under ambient pressure.

items.title: Electronic band structure reconstruction in Ni intercalated ZrTe$_2$
authors: Pedro H. A. Moya, Marli R. Cantarino, Lucas E. Correa, Leandro R. de Faria, Rodrigo M. C. Huamani, Wendell S. Silva, Claude Monney, Antonio J. S. Machado, Fernando A. Garcia
items.summary: The filling of the large van der Waals gap in Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs) often leads to lattice and electronic instabilities, which prelude the onset of a rich phenomenology. Motivated by previous results from macroscopic measurements, we investigate the electronic structure of the TMDs ZrTe$_2$ and Ni intercalated ZrTe$_2$ (Ni$_x$ZrTe$_2$, $x\approx 0.05$) employing angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). We readily identify in Ni$_x$ZrTe$_2$ two flat bands, most likely associated with localized Ni-derived 3$d$-states, at about $\approx-0.7$ eV and $\approx-1.2$ eV in binding energy. More significantly, at low $T$, we identify an electronic structure reconstruction in Ni$_x$ZrTe$_2$, which halves the electronic periodicity along the $k_{z}$ direction. This is reminiscent of a commensurate band folding with wave-vector $q=(0,0,\pi)$. A mean-field model for a charge density wave (CDW) transition driven by interband hole-hole interactions is solved with inputs from the experimentally determined electronic band structure. Comparison between theory and experiments unveils a CDW transition in Ni$_x$ZrTe$_2$, for which the gap opens above the Fermi level. Our findings invite further investigation into the structural properties of intercalated ZrTe$_2$.

items.title: AtomMOF: All-Atom Flow Matching for MOF-Adsorbate Structure Prediction
authors: Nayoung Kim, Honghui Kim, Sihyun Yu, Minkyu Kim, Seongsu Kim, Sungsoo Ahn
items.summary: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising materials for applications such as direct air capture, where performance depends on how adsorbates bind within the framework. Accurately predicting MOF-adsorbate configurations is therefore important for screening candidate materials. However, traditional approaches are computationally expensive and require a known host structure, while existing generative models rely on rigid-body assumptions and do not explicitly model adsorbates. We introduce AtomMOF, a scalable all-atom flow-matching model that jointly predicts MOF-adsorbate structures from discrete building blocks and adsorbates. Built on a Diffusion Transformer with a building block-based pairwise attention bias, AtomMOF operates in an unconstrained all-atom space and exhibits clear scaling behavior. To improve the structural validity of flexible all-atom models, we also propose Feynman-Kac (FK) steering with machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). On the BW dataset, AtomMOF achieves a 58.17% relative increase in match rate and a 31.84% relative reduction in RMSD compared with prior work. MLIP-guided steering further improves validity by 28.7% and reduces formation energy error by 86.5%. On ODAC25, AtomMOF generates adsorption configurations faster than GCMC and, when combined with MLIP relaxation, identifies lower-energy configurations than those in the reference dataset.

items.title: Tuning the magnetic properties of Kitaev materials via the antiferromagnetic proximity effect: Novel phases and application to an $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$/MnPS$_3$ bilayer
authors: Pedro M. C\^onsoli, Ezra Day-Roberts, Johannes Knolle, Antia S. Botana, Onur Erten
items.summary: In recent years, the increasing level of control over van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures has opened new routes to tune the properties of quantum materials. Motivated by these developments, we examine the potential consequences of interfacing a Kitaev honeycomb magnet, such as $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$, with a nearly lattice-matched vdW antiferromagnet. By combining perturbation theory, exact diagonalization, and a classical energy-minimization method, we show that an effective staggered magnetic field originating from the vdW antiferromagnet can drive a monolayer of a Kitaev material into various novel phases, including an antichiral Kitaev spin liquid, a nonmagnetic nematic phase, and different types of skyrmion crystals. We then apply first-principles simulations to assess the prospect of concretely realizing this setup in a heterobilayer of $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ and the easy-axis antiferromagnet MnPS$_3$.

items.title: Dissipation and microstructure in sheared active suspensions of squirmers
items.summary: We study the energy expenditure and structural correlations in semi-dilute to concentrated suspensions of squirmers using active fast Stokesian dynamics simulations. Specifically, we simulate apolar active suspensions of squirmers, or 'shakers,' and show that shear enhances the total dissipation but reduces the relative viscosity for both puller- and pusher-type shakers. At low shear rates where activity dominates, hydrodynamic interactions increase the active dissipation, more so for pullers at higher volume fractions, whereas pushers exhibit a higher viscosity, in contrast to bacterial suspensions displaying a 'superfluid' transition. At high shear rates where shear dominates, pullers and pushers behave effectively as passive spheres, generating negative normal stress differences due to shear-induced collision. Remarkably, the rate-dependent rheological responses are accompanied by unusual microstructural signatures of an enhanced nematic order and anisotropic pair correlation, both of which contribute to a higher viscosity under shear. Further simulations of self-propelled, neutral squirmers exhibit similar but weaker shear-thinning, highlighting the importance of activity over motility, underpinned by hydrodynamic interactions. Overall, our results elucidate the interplay of internal activity and external flow on the dissipation and microstructure in sheared active suspensions of squirmers.

items.title: Unifying description of competing chiral and nematic superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene
authors: Lucas Baldo, Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer
items.summary: We reveal a striking correspondence between electron- and phonon-driven pairing in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) by mapping an atomistic electronically driven pairing model onto an effective inter-valley, intra-Chern description, originally proposed for phonon-mediated superconductivity. Within the unified framework of intra-Chern pairing, we then analyze the competition between nematic and chiral $d$-wave superconducting states. The latter corresponds to the extreme Chern-polarized limit and hosts unpaired flat bands within the superconducting gap, which generally disfavors it relative to the nematic states. Crucially, nematic order is locally preferred at each momentum, but the optimal nematic directions are incompatible across the Brillouin zone due to the broken rotation symmetry. This momentum-space frustration still enables a chiral ground state at large fillings or weak interactions in a symmetric parent state. Including heterostrain or inter-valley coherence further stabilizes the nematic ground state and sets the nematic direction. Under heterostrain, this direction shows a double winding with the strain axis, revealing the $d$-wave nature of the pairing, while inter-valley coherence makes it filling dependent. Our results thereby provide a unified understanding of superconductivity in TBG, in which electron- and phonon-mediated pairing cooperate, and clarify the microscopic origin of the competition between the chiral and nematic superconducting states.

items.title: Revealing Charge Transfer in Defect-Engineered 4Hb-TaS2
authors: Siavash Karbasizadeh, Wooin Yang, Wonhee Ko, Haidong Zhou, An-Ping Li, Tom Berlijn, Sai Mu
items.summary: We present a comprehensive first-principles investigation of defects in 4$H_b$-TaS$_2$. In this layered transition metal dichalcogenide, charge transfer between alternating Mott-insulating 1T and metallic 1H layers gives rise to exotic quantum phases such as the Kondo effect and topological superconductivity. Motivated by recent defect manipulation in 4$H_b$-TaS$_2$ via STM, we address their microscopic nature and impact on interlayer charge transfer. To this end, we systematically analyze over 90 defects using large-scale density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Our analysis identifies 1H sulfur vacancies, Ta-on-S antisites, and Ta interstitials as the most likely origins of the commonly observed defects, with Ta-on-S antisites producing the strongest charge-transfer modulation. Our extensive dataset, compiled from STM simulations, defect formation energies, work functions, and charge transfer, establishes a foundational resource for future theoretical and experimental studies on defect engineering in 4$H_b$-TaS$_2$.

items.title: Topological multicomponent superconductivity with sizable $s$-wave admixture in twisted bilayer cuprates
authors: Yu-Hang Li, Congjun Wu, Wang Yang
items.summary: We investigate multicomponent superconductivity in twisted bilayer cuprates with order parameter $s+d_1 e^{i\phi_1}+d_2 e^{i\phi_2}$, where $s=s_1+s_2$ is the layer-symmetric $s$-wave pairing and $d_i$ is the $d$-wave pairing in layer $i$. When $\phi_1-\phi_2\neq 0,\pi$, this three-component state spontaneously breaks time-reversal and $C_4$ rotational symmetries and can realize a topologically nontrivial phase. Ginzburg-Landau analysis and self-consistent mean-field calculations show that this state is stabilized over a broad parameter regime. We further identify nematic Kerr anisotropy as a key signature distinguishing it from $s+id$ and $d_1+e^{i\phi}d_2$, and find that its Josephson critical current remains sizable near the $45^{\circ}$ twist. Our results show that $s$-wave pairing does not preclude chiral topological superconductivity, pointing to twisted cuprates as a more robust platform than previously appreciated.

items.title: Dilute Zn alloying in biodegradable Mg wires: microstructure, mechanical performance, and degradation behavior
authors: Ji\v{r}\'i Ryj\'a\v{c}ek, Leonard Hlod\'ak, Ji\v{r}\'i Li\v{s}ka, Jan Pinc, Tom\'a\v{s} Herma, Karel Tesa\v{r}
items.summary: Dilute Mg-Zn wires are of great interest for biodegradable small-bone fixation, as magnesium degradation can support bone-related processes, while low zinc additions may provide biological benefits without compromising biocompatibility. In this work, the influence of Zn content below the room-temperature solubility limit was assessed in Mg-Zn wires intended for resorbable implant applications. Mg-0.4Zn, Mg-0.6Zn, Mg-0.8Zn, and Mg-1.5Zn alloys were processed by single-step direct hot extrusion into thin wires and characterized by correlative microstructural analysis, tensile testing, bending experiments, and in vitro degradation. All compositions achieved a recrystallized fine equiaxed grain size of 5.0-5.9 um and exhibited ultimate tensile strengths of 246-256 MPa with elongations of 23-28 %. In these thin wires, Zn content had only a limited effect on grain size, tensile properties, and bending behavior, although lower-Zn alloys showed a pronounced sharp yield point. Bending was governed mainly by extrusion texture and preserved reversible plasticity through twinning and detwinning. Simulated body fluid caused rapid localized degradation and loss of mechanical integrity within 7 days, while the biologically more relevant DMEM-based medium better reflected the expected in vivo response. Together, these findings support dilute Mg-Zn wires as a simple material platform for the development of future resorbable bone fixation devices.

items.title: Limitations of Debye-Waller lattice temperature extraction under electronic excitation
authors: N. Medvedev, M. Kopecky, J. Chalupsky, L. Juha
items.summary: Ultrafast diffraction is the cutting-edge technique to extract the atomic temperature at femtosecond timescales, and further related quantities - in particular, electron-phonon coupling strength at elevated electronic temperatures. The present work demonstrates limitations of such an analysis, emphasizing the importance of careful evaluation of the evolution of the Debye temperature. It is shown that, due to the sensitivity of the Debye-Waller analysis to this parameter, neglecting its changes under electronic excitation may lead to significant deviations of the atomic temperature extracted from its true values.

items.title: A method for calculating entropy production without knowing transition rates or dwell times
items.summary: The entropy production rate is central to the study of non-equilibrium systems. This parameter is closely connected to violation of time-reversal symmetry, energy consumption, efficiency, and other properties of interest; in short, it quantifies how far a system is from thermodynamic equilibrium. Standard formulas for the entropy production require knowledge of the system's underlying dynamics, but this knowledge may be hard to acquire in practice. Here, I present a method for inferring the entropy production rate of a Markovian system from the sequence of states that the system occupies on a single long trajectory or many shorter trajectories, and the total time of the trajectory or trajectories. The method does not require knowledge of the dwell times in the various states, the times at which transitions occur, or of the transition rates characterizing the Markov process.

items.title: Stabilizing the parquet problem
authors: Herbert E{\ss}l, Stefan Rohshap, Marcel Gievers, Markus Wallerberger, Alessandro Toschi, Anna Kauch
items.summary: We systematically analyze the stability of the iterative solution of the parquet equations by studying the spectrum of the Jacobian associated with the commonly used damped fixed-point iteration procedure. In this context, we provide an explicit criterion that determines when the physical fixed point of the parquet iteration becomes unstable. Importantly, we demonstrate that misleading convergence issues, observed in parquet calculations at intermediate-to-high interaction values, are not restricted to parameter regions where the two-particle irreducible vertex diverges, but can also arise in absence of vertex divergences. Hence, the misleading convergence issues of parquet-based algorithms are not directly caused by the crossings of two solutions of the (multivalued) Luttinger-Ward functional, that are associated with vertex divergences. Building on these insights, we apply the controlled stabilization strategy of Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016502 (2026) to the challenging case of the parquet iteration. This strategy allows the convergence to the physical solution in the instability regimes. We apply this procedure to the zero-point model and the Hubbard model in the atomic limit, where we successfully stabilize the physical solution deep in the non-perturbative regime, even across multiple divergence lines. Further, we compare our stabilization strategy to alternative fixed-point solvers that can be used to solve the parquet problem.

items.title: Chirality-induced spin selectivity due to an emergent molecular orbital moment
authors: Sumit Ghosh, Angela Wittmann, Frank Matthes, Daniel E. B\"urgler
items.summary: The microscopic origin of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS), a phenomena where chiral molecules connected to a magnetic electrode show large spin-dependent conductance asymmetry even in ambient temperature, still remains an open question. Most of the existent theories are based on some sort of effective spin-orbit coupling or interfacial scattering, which do not provide satisfactory explanations for experimental observations such as the magnitude of spin polarization or the length dependence of the effect. We propose an alternative theoretical framework rooted in an intrinsic molecular contribution that shows a robust CISS effect and scales with the length of the molecule. The mechanism is based on the emergent molecular magnetic moment (MOM), which can produce experimentally observed point-symmetric I-V curves without violating the Onsager-Casimir reciprocity relation. The MOM has an intrinsic component that is governed by the chirality of the molecule and leads to finite CISS magnetoresistance and magnetochiral conductance asymmetry (MChA) that are even in bias voltage. By decomposing the MOM into its Fermi sea and Fermi surface components, we show that under strong bias, the MOM can be dominated by the Fermi surface contribution, which causes a sign change in the MChA leading to a behavior similar to that of electric magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA). Finally, we analyze the effect of a magnetic field within the same framework, which may provide better insight into the crossover between CISS and eMChA.

items.title: Approximating velocity fields with planted point attractors via Neural-ODE for classification purposes
authors: Feliciano Giuseppe Pacifico, Duccio Fanelli, Lorenzo Buffoni, Lorenzo Chicchi, Diego Febbe, Raffaele Marino
items.summary: In this work, Neural ODEs equipped with a curated collection of equilibrium points have been successfully employed for classification tasks. The planted fixed points serve as indicators for the target classes, while the velocity field, leveraging the universal approximation capabilities of the architecture, shapes the dynamical landscape. This process defines the basins of attraction of the trained model, effectively directing each input (provided as an initial condition) toward its corresponding destination target.

items.title: Analyzing the Gelation Transition through Fractional Viscoelasticity and the Mittag-Leffler-Prabhakar Function
items.summary: The gelation transition, a process that transforms a flowable liquid into an elastic solid, occurs in a variety of systems, ranging from colloidal to polymeric. During the gelation transition, a system passes through a critical gel state characterized by scale-free power-law viscoelasticity. Interestingly, the fractional calculus provides a natural mathematical language for such power-law viscoelasticity. In this work, we develop physically constrained fractional viscoelastic models, as well as those based on the three-parameter Mittag-Leffler-Prabhakar function, for both the pre-gel and post-gel regimes, ensuring consistency with the conventional scaling relations in each regime. While the fractional pre-gel model is observed to be valid only for a restricted subset of parameter values, the Prabhakar function-based model for the relaxation modulus, which translates into a Havriliak-Negami function-based complex modulus, rigorously removes this limitation. We enforce continuity of the dynamic moduli and their derivatives across the critical gel point, which universally imposes a symmetry in the relaxation dynamics on either side of the critical gel state. Such enforcement further validates the hyperscaling relation connecting the critical exponents, making it a theoretical necessity rather than an empirical coincidence. We validate the proposed models against time- and frequency-domain experimental data. A model-agnostic, frequency-independent rheological fingerprint of the critical gel state, uniquely determined by two critical exponents, is also identified.

items.title: Driven square lattice of quantum dots in a magnetic field coupled to a cylindrical FIR-photon cavity
authors: Vidar Gudmundsson, Vram Mughnetsyan, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Jeng-Da Chai, Nzar Rauf Abdullah, Chi-Shung Tang, Wen-Hsuan Kuan, Valeriu Moldoveanu, Andrei Manolescu
items.summary: We present a comprehensive computational study of driven quantum dot arrays in a square lattice configuration, subject to an external magnetic field and coupled to a cylindrical far-infrared photon cavity. The driving is introduced through a harmonic modulation of the full electron-photon interaction, therefore including both paramagnetic and diamagnetic contributions. The electron-electron Coulomb interactions are treated within density functional theory, while the electron-photon coupling is modeled using a many-body configuration interaction approach at each iteration of the density functional. By exploiting the unique properties of the cylindrical TE$_{011}$ cavity mode, we demonstrate selective enhancement of diamagnetic two-photon transitions. Our results reveal that the effectiveness of harmonic modulation of the electron-photon interaction is strongly dependent on both the driving frequency and the electron occupation number per dot. When the driving frequency approaches twice the cavity photon frequency, the system exhibits resonant behavior characterized by efficient photon pumping, occupation of higher-order photon replicas, and activation of collective radial Coulomb breathing modes. These findings establish a controllable mechanism for manipulating photon states in coupled quantum dot-cavity systems and provide insights into the interplay among harmonic modulation, photonic excitations, magnetic confinement, and many-body electron correlations in dimensionally reduced nanostructures.

items.title: Weakly Nonlinear Analysis of Jammed Solids
authors: Kota Noto, Harukuni Ikeda, Kuniyasu Saitoh, Hisao Hayakawa
items.summary: We investigate the structural evolution in jammed solids by analyzing the eigenmodes of a generalized Hessian matrix that incorporates spatial modulation via wave numbers. Unlike the conventional Hessian, this generalized formulation captures linearly unstable modes through a Fourier-based extension of the Hessian matrix, enabling us to study responses beyond the mechanically stable regime. We demonstrate that the excitation of unstable eigenmodes leads to structural rearrangements independent of the initial perturbation by the simulation. Furthermore, we derive a weakly nonlinear amplitude equation to describe the growth and saturation of these unstable modes, analogous to the Landau equation. Our framework provides a pathway to understand instability-driven configuration changes in disordered solids.

items.title: Machine Learning Assisted Design of Complex and High Entropy Alloys by Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD Process for Low Carbon Energy Applications in Extreme Environments
authors: Paul Foulquier, Ryma Haddad, Ali Mahmoud, Eric Monsifrot, Fanny Balbaud-Celerier, Jean-Philippe Poli, Frederic Schuster
items.summary: Complex and high entropy alloys are attracting much attention currently thanks to their mechanical and corrosion resistance properties in harsh environments, in particular needed for carbon-free energy applications. However, their elaboration in bulk and in thin film form in a trial-and-error approach is impractical due to their complexity and the cocktail effect. The recent development of artificial intelligence brings a new possibility for their elaboration and adjustment of their properties. Firstly, we present an overview of Materials and data science research. Then we describe how DIADEM - French initiative for Materials and Data science convergence - tackles the development of innovative coatings for carbon-free energy applications (nuclear, high temperature electrolysis, ...) thanks to the development of a nationwide network of synthesis and characterization platforms - the DIADEM discovery hub. We describe in particular DIADEM-2D, an AI-driven Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD process using 4 cathodes in confocal combinatorial configuration. We present the high entropy alloy determination using data from the literature for corrosion resistance in molten salt media and nuclear accidental conditions. An element-independent model gathering deposition parameters and coating properties has been implemented allowing the design of protective coatings with a particular composition. We demonstrate the feasibility of this process and its accuracy.

items.title: An LLM agent for end-to-end computational materials discovery
authors: Chen Yuntong, Huang Lijiang, Li Yingqi, Liu Yu, Zhao Dan, Sun Mingqi, Ju Chentian, Liu Yanbing, Li Xiao-Yan, Zhao Guobin
items.summary: Coordinating multi-scale tasks is an effective strategy for computational materials discovery, yet the diverse algorithms and tools involved make this process highly challenging. Here we present DREAMS, a large language model (LLM)-based agent system capable of executing the entire screening pipeline for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). DREAMS processes a large body of MOF literature, links publications to their crystal structures, and curates them into a computation-ready database, which is then screened with progressively more expensive simulations. The promising candidates identified for separation under wet flue gas conditions all originate from independent studies. By bridging the heterogeneous stages from literature mining to high-throughput simulation, DREAMS operates across application domains and enables even non-experts to discover high-performance materials in an end-to-end, automated manner.

items.title: Visualizing Chiral Edge Modes in Twisted Cuprate Superconductors via Scanning-Probe Quantum Sensing
authors: Senlei Li, Xiaomeng Cui, Renzhi Sun, Lingjie Zhou, Yiran Zhao, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Genda Gu, Hailong Wang, Kartiek Agarwal, Philip Kim, Chunhui Rita Du
items.summary: Recently, unconventional superconductivity hosted by twisted van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures has received immense interest due to the exotic pairing symmetry, electronic interactions and nontrivial topological nature that are naturally relevant to the fast-advancing quantum technologies. Here, we report scanning-probe quantum sensing of nanoscale electromagnetic behaviors of twisted vdW cuprate superconductors. Using single-spin relaxometry, we directly visualize edge modes spontaneously formed in twisted Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (BSCCO). By investigating temperature dependent variations of edge-state-induced quantum spin relaxation, we experimentally evaluate the magnitude of nontrivial topological band gap opened at nodal points in twisted BSCCO and its critical temperature behaviors under different twist angles. We further observe alternating chiral domains defined by edge modes, exploring experimental signatures of in-plane magnetic field-induced topology in 45{\deg} twisted BSCCO. Our results advance the current understanding of twisted vdW nodal superconductors, presenting an appealing high-temperature topological superconducting material platform for cutting-edge quantum innovation.

items.title: Laser-induced metastable (anti-)skyrmion states with higher-order topological charge
authors: Tim Titze (University of G\"ottingen, Germany and), Marcel M\"oller (Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, G\"ottingen, Germany and), Timo Schmidt (University of Augsburg, Germany and), Mariam Hassan (University of Augsburg, Germany and), Sabri Koraltan (Technical University of Vienna, Austria and), Stefan Mathias (University of G\"ottingen, Germany and, ICASEC, University of G\"ottingen, Germany), Manfred Albrecht (University of Augsburg, Germany and), Claus Ropers (University of G\"ottingen, Germany and, ICASEC, University of G\"ottingen, Germany), Daniel Steil (University of G\"ottingen, Germany and)
items.summary: Ultrafast creation and manipulation of topologically non-trivial spin objects promises significant potential for spintronic applications. Here, we demonstrate laser-induced nucleation of skyrmions and antiskyrmions with topological charge up to $|Q|=3$ from the saturated magnetization state of a Co/Ni-multilayer which does not intrinsically host a skyrmionic ground state. The resulting configuration of spin objects thus constitutes a metastable, thermodynamically hidden magnetic state. We control the number and type of spin objects by the excitation fluence and the external out-of-plane magnetic field.

items.title: Unmodeled states and uncertain action outcomes in agentic scanning tunneling microscopy
authors: Siyu Cheng, Muxian Xu, Christopher Candelora, Ilija Zeljkovic
items.summary: In physical experiments, interventions can alter hidden experimental states in ways that cannot be predicted in advance. Autonomous scientific agents must therefore interpret the consequences of their interventions while operating with incomplete knowledge of the experimental state. Here we investigate this problem using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) tip conditioning, traditionally a human-expert-intensive task governed by inaccessible tip apex conditions and uncertain action outcomes. We introduce quailbot, an agent harness that places the LLM inside the instrument feedback loop by linking physical interventions with experimental readbacks. After a brief apprenticeship with a human expert, frontier LLM agents autonomously completed end-to-end tip conditioning on an STM and passed an independent verification. The contingencies that arose during the experiments further exposed the limits of LLM agentic autonomy when relevant experimental states or dynamics were hidden or unmodeled. Our results show that future autonomous physical experimentation requires agents to infer hidden and unmodeled experimental states, track the outcomes of their actions, and operate within the observability and action limits of real instruments.

items.title: Closed analytical form of many-body free volume and thermodynamics of monodisperse hard disks
authors: Victor M. Pergamenshchik, Taras Bryk, Andrij Trokhymchuk
items.summary: The hard disk model is a fundamental reference system for excluded volume physics, liquid structure, and 2D ordering. Yet, despite its apparent simplicity, an analytical formulation of its thermodynamics has remained difficult because the free volume available to disks centers has a highly nontrivial many-body geometry. Here we show that this geometry admits a closed and exact representation: for any given hard disk configuration, the free volume can be analytically expressed through intersection areas of up to five exclusion disks. This provides a direct geometrical route from particle coordinates to the configurational partition function and entropy. We prove that the N disk partition function factorizes into a product of conditional free volumes and identify its two limiting asymptotic forms: the low density fluid regime controlled by extensive cavities and the high density fluid regime controlled by intensive private cells. Using the geometric measures computed from representative equilibrium particle configurations, the resulting theory reproduces the established hard disk equation of state over almost the entire density range up to close packing. At intermediate densities, the analysis reveals a mixed fluid regime in which localized caged defects provide an additional configurational entropy within the density interval preceding liquid hexatic coexistence. Finally, the five disk intersection area is shown to be a sensitive local scalar measure of hexagonal ordering, complementing the orientational order parameter and emphasizing the central role of many-body correlations.

items.title: A neural density functional for polymer electrolytes with exact structure and transferable Coulomb coupling
items.summary: Ion correlations set the structure of polymer electrolytes and depend on the host permittivity, which is low and varies between polymers. A functional that carries these correlations from molecular simulations to larger inhomogeneous systems must transfer across domain sizes, geometries and coupling strengths. We introduce a neural density functional for the ions of a salt-doped polymer melt with built-in integrability, continuous spatial symmetry, the Noether identities, perfect screening in stable bulk states, and parameters that refer to no grid or box. The permittivity enters only through the Bjerrum length, an explicit argument constrained by an exact relation: the free-energy derivative with respect to the Bjerrum length is the Coulomb correlation energy. Trained by force matching on planar profiles at five Bjerrum lengths spanning 8-30 monomer diameters, the functional predicts, without retraining, density profiles in fourfold longer boxes and under two-dimensional fields, bulk structure factors and the long-wavelength number response, also at a concentration and a permittivity left out of training. It reproduces this energy identity on Coulomb energies that never enter the training. Its nonlinear density dependence captures correlations that a quadratic pair closure misses: the number response grows several-fold with concentration, and at low concentration the coupling lowers it through ion association, below the ideal value at the strongest coupling, while the host sets it in the concentrated melt. At fixed coupling, it is more accurate than three neural architectures and loses little accuracy with a quarter of the training data.

items.title: Constructing Large and Structured Decoherence-Free Subspaces in Hybrid Quantum Systems
authors: Catalin-Mihai Halati, Tony Jin, Roderich Moessner
items.summary: We develop a framework to construct large decoherence-free subspaces with a nontrivial structure. The construction is based on hybrid quantum systems in which quantum matter is coupled to a dissipative bosonic mode. Dissipation imposes a global constraint on the matter by selecting the matter null states in the long-time limit. The decoherence-free subspaces spanned by matter null states can exhibit exotic quantum properties and emergent symmetries that do not characterize the full Liouvillian dynamics. We show how to construct many-body operators with physically interesting null states by employing representation theory of Lie algebras. This approach allows us to choose models based on their underlying algebraic structure. We consider explicitly the example of coupling a lossy optical cavity to the directed tunneling operator in one-dimension. In this case, the symmetries of the decoherence-free subspace originate in an $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$ algebra, leading to an exponentially large number of steady states. We characterize the null states for both fermionic and bosonic particles, employing analytical and numerical methods. The states exhibit several properties that underline their complex quantum nature: long-range kinetic correlations and volume-law entanglement. The nonreciprocal nature of the directed tunneling dynamics leads to the emergence in the many-body regime of a symmetry-constrained Liouvillian skin effect. The open light-matter system exhibits a strong symmetry stemming from spinless $\eta$-pairing algebras. We show how the nontrivial properties emerge in the dissipative dynamics from generic initial states, by performing the quantum evolution of the hybrid open system with time-dependent matrix product state. Our framework opens avenues for dissipatively engineering complex quantum correlations and harnessing nonreciprocity in a controlled manner.

items.title: Universal Boolean Computation in Negatively Coupled Circle Map Lattices
authors: Priyanka D. Bhoyar, Prashant M. Gade
items.summary: We investigate the computational capabilities of a one-dimensional lattice of negatively coupled circle maps in its traveling wave regime. We interpret propagating waves as information carriers and exploit their interactions to implement Boolean logic. The logical states are encoded by the propagation direction of the traveling waves, while the presence or absence of a wave at a designated output location represents the logical output. Using controlled wave collisions, we demonstrate the realization of NAND and NOR gates along with other basic gates. Since NAND and NOR operations are functionally complete, the results establish that the traveling wave regime of the negatively coupled circle-map lattice supports universal Boolean computation in principle. The demonstrated logical operations remain valid over a finite range of the coupling strength \epsilon and map parameter \omega, indicating robustness of the computational scheme to parameter variations. Our results therefore demonstrate that computational functionality can emerge from the collective nonlinear dynamics of a coupled map lattice, providing a con- nection between the dynamical properties of traveling wave states and collision based information processing.

items.title: Solubility of poorly soluble species in bulk and nanopores from grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling
authors: Russell Kajouri, Adyant Agrawal, Philipp St\"ark, Alexander Schlaich, Christian Holm
items.summary: Poorly soluble species can have mean populations below one in small systems such as nanopores. In this regime, the grand-potential minimum, which identifies the most probable particle number, differs from the ensemble-averaged solute loading. We use grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling (GCWLS) to calculate the density of states $\Omega(N_\mathrm{A}, N_\mathrm{B})$ for a binary Lennard-Jones mixture of solute B in solvent A, both in bulk and in slit pores. One set of GCWLS simulations gives ensemble averages over a range of chemical potentials, whereas conventional grand-canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulation requires a separate simulation at each state point. Independent GCMC simulations confirm the GCWLS ensemble averages. The solvent number distribution is nearly Gaussian, whereas the dilute solute distribution is skewed and Poisson-like. The most probable solute number therefore lies below the ensemble-averaged loading $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle$ and is zero whenever $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle<1$. Reading the solute loading from the grand-potential minimum underestimates it and can falsely indicate that no solute is present. Defining the oversolubility as $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}=x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{conf}}/x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$, where $x_\mathrm{B}$ is the solute mole fraction, we find $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}\approx12$ in a pore of 3.5 particle diameters width when both wall interactions are repulsive. Adding wall-solute attraction moderately raises it to $\approx13$, whereas wall-solvent attraction lowers it to $\approx3.4$. This comparison shows that the wall-solvent interaction controls most of the enhancement. As the pore widens, $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}$ decreases toward unity. In bulk and in nanopores alike, the solubility of poorly soluble species should be obtained from ensemble averages rather than from grand-potential minima.

items.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
authors: Andre M. Sonnet, Epifanio G. Virga
items.summary: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

items.title: Geometry-controlled zeros of resonant Kelvin-wave conversion in four spatial dimensions
authors: Wei-can Yang, Xiang-dong Xu, Cheng Li, Ke-yu Lu
items.summary: Geometry can suppress leading Kelvin-wave conversion even at exact momentum and frequency resonance. We demonstrate this on a vortex surface in four spatial dimensions. Perpendicular incidence removes the complete local-area four-wave coupling, exposing the finite nonlocal interaction carried by the surrounding fluid. Reflection keeps the quartets exactly resonant as their wave-number ratio varies. The flow restores conversion at generic ratios but develops a sign-changing zero of its own. Matching the complete Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) four-wave coupling establishes microscopic zeros whose ratios approach $\lambda_*\simeq 1.469$ at long wavelengths. Finite-domain GP calculations exhibit the sign reversal. Separate coherent-mixing and probe calculations relate the coupling sign to the generated-wave phase and the frequency ordering of reflection-even and reflection-odd modes. The result isolates a nonlinear effect of the surrounding flow and provides a phase-sensitive test of vortex dynamics beyond local tension.

items.title: Framework to identify defect-insensitive electron transport in topological semimetals
authors: Lily Jade Joyce, Michelle M. Kelley, Timothy Philicelli, Ching-Tzu Chen, Ravishankar Sundararaman
items.summary: Topological semimetals are of increasing interest to replace conventional metals for interconnects in future semiconductor chips, due to their potential to exhibit decreasing resistivity with reducing wire dimensions and a lower sensitivity to electron scattering at defects. First-principles evaluation of promising topological semimetals for interconnects typically employ non-equilibrium Green's functions (NEGF) techniques to estimate defect scattering, but such calculations for specific defect geometries are difficult to systematize and compare between disparate materials. Here, we develop an NEGF-based approach to systematically and rapidly evaluate the defect sensitivity of electron transport in materials without depending on material-specific defect geometries. Specifically, we analyze the eigen-spectrum of the transmission matrix for an incoherent ensemble of all-possible single-atom vacancy defects, which clearly reveals eigenvalues close to 1 for defect-insensitive transport modes. Applied to the leading candidates, we show that this robustness to defect scattering is extremely sensitive to surface orientation and Fermi level for each material. We find nearly-perfect insensitivity to defects only for wavevectors with single transport modes within specific Fermi level ranges in CoSi(001) and PtAl(001). Importantly, we also find high insensitivity for certain non-isolated modes in NbAs that emerge specifically due to spin-orbit coupling; these modes could not be identified previously as they were buried in the total transmission. These non-isolated modes have been buried in previous studies of total transmission, and can now be directly compared to other materials due to our standardization of defect-creation. This technique improves the state-of-the-art NEGF method and enables unbiased evaluation of future topological semimetal candidates for nanoscale interconnects.

items.title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
items.summary: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like $1s^22s^2$ sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor $D_0=\sqrt{1+\delta^2}$. Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

items.title: Cell size heterogeneity controls crystallization of the developing fruit fly wing
authors: Kartik Chhajed, Franz S. Gruber, Rapha\"el Etournay, Natalie A. Dye, Frank J\"ulicher, Marko Popovi\'c
items.summary: -cross Abstract: A fundamental question in biology is to understand how patterns and shapes emerge from the collective interplay of large numbers of cells. Cells forming two-dimensional epithelial tissues behave as active materials that undergo remodeling and spontaneous shape changes. Focusing on the fly wing as a model system, we find that the cellular packing in the wing epithelium transitions from a disordered packing to an ordered, crystalline packing. While previous studies propose a role of tissue shear flow in establishing the ordered cell packing in the fly wing, we reveal a role of cell size heterogeneity. Indeed, we find that even if tissue shear have been inhibited, cell packings in the fruit fly wing epithelium transition from disordered to an ordered packing. We propose that the transition is controlled by the cell size heterogeneity, which is quantified by the cell size polydispersity. To explore the role of cell size polydispersity in controlling cellular packings, we implement polydispersity in a vertex model of epithelial tissues. Through numerical simulations of this model, we show that there is a critical value of cell size polydispersity above which cellular packings are disordered and below which they form a crystalline packing. By analyzing experimental data, we find that cell size polydispersity decreases during fly wing development. The observed dynamics of tissue crystallisation is consistent with the slow ordering kinetics we observe in the vertex model. Therefore, although tissue shear does not control the transition, it significantly enhances the rate of tissue-scale ordering by facilitating alignment of locally ordered crystallites. Our results identify cell size heterogeneity as a control parameter, in both the vertex model and the fruit fly wing epithelium, controlling the transition between ordered and disordered cellular packings.

items.title: Succession of Ising criticality and its threshold in critical quantum Ising model subject to $X+ZZ$ decoherence
authors: Yoshihito Kuno, Takahiro Orito, Ikuo Ichinose
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We investigate a mixed state quantum criticality in the Ising model under $X+ZZ$ decoherence. In the doubled Hilbert space formalism, the decohered state resides on the self-dual critical line of the quantum Ashkin-Teller (qAT) model, as a result of the specific choice of the decoherence channel. On the other hand, since the mixed state under $X+ZZ$ decoherence satisfies the Kramers-Wannier self-duality in a weak sense, the Ising criticality of the pure state can be partially preserved in the mixed system. By making use of the combination of the doubled Hilbert space formalism and matrix product states, a numerical study is carried out. We numerically find that, up to moderate decoherence strength, the behavior of the mixed states on the critical line is consistent with Ising-like scaling within the accessible system sizes, with the effective central charge and critical exponents close to the Ising-CFT values $c=1/2$, $\eta=1/4$, and $\eta_X=2$. Our results of the central charge and critical exponents contradict the ones in the $c=1$ orbifold boson CFT describing the critical state of the qAT model. In addition, we also numerically observe the flow of the central charge up to strong decoherence. The strong decoherence washes out the remnant Ising criticality and induces strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking.

items.title: Thermoelastic wave-based logic for mechanically cognitive materials
authors: Ethan Fort, Mohamed Mousa, Mostafa Nouh
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Recent advances in metamaterials and fabrication techniques have revived interest in mechanical computing. Contrary to techniques relying on static deformations of buckling beams or origami-based lattices, the integration of wave scattering and mechanical memory presents a promising path toward efficient, low-latency elastoacoustic computing. This work introduces a novel class of multifunctional mechanical computing circuits that leverage the rich dynamics of phononic and locally resonant materials. These circuits incorporate memory-integrated components, realized here via metamaterial cells infused with shape memory alloys which recall stored elastic profiles and trigger specific actions upon thermal activation. A critical advantage of this realization is its synergistic interaction with incident vibroacoustic loads and the inherited high speed of waves, as opposed to recent adaptations of mechanically intelligent systems that employ innately slower mechanisms such as elastomeric shape changes and snap-through bistabilities. Through a proof-of-concept physical implementation, the efficacy and reconfigurability of the wave-based gates are demonstrated via output probes and measured wavefields. Furthermore, the modular design of the fundamental gates can be used as building blocks to construct complex combinational logic circuits, paving the way for sequential logic in wave-based analog computing systems.

items.title: Testing Transformer Learnability on the Arithmetic Sequence of Rooted Trees
authors: Alessandro Breccia, Federica Gerace, Marco Lippi, Gabriele Sicuro, Pierluigi Contucci
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We study whether a transformer network can learn the deterministic sequence of trees generated by the iterated prime factorization of the natural numbers. Each integer is mapped into a rooted planar tree and the resulting sequence $\mathbb{N}\mathscr{T}$ defines an arithmetic text with measurable statistical structure. A transformer network (the GPT-2 architecture) is trained from scratch on the first $10^{11}$ elements and evaluated on next-token prediction and masked-token prediction tasks, with a Hidden Markov Model as baseline and a scaling analysis over context window, dataset size, vocabulary size and model size. The model reaches a word accuracy of about $0.4$, well above the baseline, and its performance remains stable on test blocks located at $10^{13}$-$10^{15}$, far beyond the training interval. Moreover, the likelihood assigned by the trained model separates the arithmetic text from two controls: synthetic token sequences that preserve the marginal token frequencies but not their order, with a separation that widens with the context, and sequences containing more than three consecutive square-free integers, a configuration that arithmetic forbids. These results indicate that the transformer captures regularities of the arithmetic text that go beyond its frequency profile.

items.title: Arbitrary-order exceptional points in a nanomechanical cavity
authors: Ning Wu, Kaiyu Cui, Ziming Chen, Chenxuan Wang, Xue Feng, Fang Liu, Wei Zhang, Hao Sun, Yongzhuo Li, Yidong Huang
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian spectral singularities, shape the evolution dynamics ranging from topological mode control to high-precision sensing. Higher-order EPs unlock enriched and sharpened spectral topology beyond the minimal second-order counterpart, thus expanding capabilities in those domains. However, the intrinsic topological fragility of higher-order EPs has long hindered their robust experimental realization. Here, we present a scalable architecture that implements arbitrary-order EPs via an optically mediated recurrent network comprising a single nanomechanical resonator and an ensemble of digital synthetic resonators. We experimentally validate this architecture's scalability for both linear and nonlinear mechanical EPs, demonstrating EPs up to the seventh order. Moreover, we reveal that the fundamental noise component, in contrast to some technical-noise contributions, shares the same system coupling channel and undergoes identical root-response amplification as the measured signal. The co-amplification mechanism sets the fundamental sensitivity limit near EPs of any order, as verified by direct signal-to-noise ratio measurements. Our work establishes a general platform for exploring higher-order EP-based phenomena while clarifying the fundamental boundary of non-Hermitian sensitivity enhancement. More broadly, it facilitates a connection between non-Hermitian physics and AI-inspired recurrent architectures across diverse physical systems.

items.title: Open quantum spin chains with non-reciprocity: a theoretical approach based on the time-dependent generalized Gibbs ensemble
authors: Alice March\'e, Hironobu Yoshida, Alberto Nardin, Hosho Katsura, Leonardo Mazza
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We study an open quantum spin chain with non-reciprocal dissipation using a theoretical approach known as time-dependent generalized Gibbs ensemble. In the regime of weak dissipation the system is fully characterized by its rapidity distribution and we derive a closed set of coupled differential equations governing their time evolution. We check the accuracy of this theory by benchmarking the results against numerical simulations. Using this framework we are able to compute both the magnetization density and current dynamics, identifying some relations between the two. The problem of the anomalous power-law exponents identified in a previous work is discussed. Our work constitutes a theoretical approach that is able to describe the physics of non-reciprocal open quantum spin chains beyond analyses based on non-interacting fermions.

items.title: Eigenstate condensation in quantum systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces
authors: Christopher David White, Michael Winer, Noam Bernstein
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Random quantum states drawn from the Haar ensemble with a constraint on the energy expectation value $E_{\mathrm{av}} = \langle \psi | H | \psi\rangle$ display \textit{eigenstate condensation}: for $E_{\mathrm{av}}$ below a critical value $E_c$, they develop macroscopic overlap with the ground state. We study eigenstate condensation in systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. These systems display three phases: a ground-state phase, in which energy-constrained random states have macroscopic overlap with the ground state; a high-temperature phase, in which they have exponentially small overlap with each energy eigenstate; and an anti-ground-state phase, in which they have macroscopic overlap with the most highly excited state. In local spin systems the ground-state and anti-ground-state phases approach the middle of the spectrum as $1/[\text{system size}]$, but -- because the condensation phase transitions have exponential, rather than polynomial, finite-size scaling -- the crossover becomes exponentially sharp in system size and the high-temperature phase is best understood as an extended phase.

items.title: Convex Analysis of Relaxation Dynamics in Chemical Reaction Networks and Generalized Gradient Flows
authors: Keisuke Sugie, Dimitri Loutchko, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We obtain bounds on the Kullback--Leibler divergence to equilibrium for mass-action chemical reaction networks (CRNs) with equilibrium. The associated trajectory-dependent bounds are characterized in terms of the singular values of the stoichiometric matrix, convexity parameters, and time-integrated activities via deformed-exponential-type functions. We further extend these bounds within a generalized gradient flow framework. We highlight the biological relevance of this framework: the resulting bounds apply to quasi-steady-state regimes, where long transients and plateau-like behavior are common and functionally important. We illustrate the framework using a catalytic CRN exhibiting plateaus, where the bounds provide an a posteriori characterization of slow relaxation induced by local convexity and provide a bound-based approach to quantifying relaxation in CRNs.

items.title: Neural networks become centroid classifiers when trained on heavily corrupted inputs
authors: Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, Omri Lesser
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Learning from imperfect data is a central theme in machine learning, connecting practical questions of robustness to fundamental questions of learnability. Here we examine attribute noise: learning from corrupted inputs while keeping the labels intact, a setting that has received considerably less analytical attention than its label-noise counterpart. We consider two types of corruption models: additive noise and replacement noise. Through experiments with multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) on corrupted classification datasets, we find that neural networks remain robust, maintaining well-above-chance accuracy even when inputs are >90% corrupted -- far beyond human recognition. To understand this robustness, we analyze infinite-width networks in the heavy-corruption regime using a mean-field-inspired approach and derive a leading-order decision rule for the classification outcome: the network implements a prototype rule, the nearest-class-mean, assigning each test point to the class whose training-set average it most closely resembles. This leading-order decision rule is universal across a broad range of MLP architectures, holding for any depth, as well as a wide class of activation functions and noise distributions. The same centroid mechanism closely matches finite-width network behavior in our experiments and provides an interpretable and analytically tractable account of why learning can succeed even when individual training examples carry almost no signal.

items.title: Interpreting Liouvillian Eigenmodes: Quantized Orbits in Dissipative Systems
authors: Ashlin V Thomas, Felix Fritzsch, Masudul Haque, Shovan Dutta
