By projecting a tilted massive Dirac model onto a single low-energy band, we construct a composite-boson Chern--Simons theory for the lowest Landau level that retains projection-induced nonlinear electromagnetic couplings. The nonlinear Hall resistivity vanishes in the dc limit, while its finite-frequency response retains the characteristic filling-factor dependence $ρ^{(2)}_{TLL}\proptoν^{-2}$, where $ν$ is the Landau-level filling factor. At low frequency, its real and imaginary parts scale as $(ω/ω_c)^2$ and $ω/ω_c$, respectively, where $ω_c$ is the cyclotron frequency, and the response is strongly anisotropic with respect to the crystalline tilt axis. Notably, the Kohn-mode resonances present in the second-order conductivity cancel in the nonlinear Hall resistivity. These results establish finite-frequency nonlinear transport as a bulk probe of fractional quantum Hall fluids without requiring nonlinear edge-mode dispersion.

items.title: From Simulation to Experiment: Benchmarking Machine-Learning Models for Quantum-Dot State Recognition
items.summary: Machine-learning models for quantum-dot state recognition are commonly trained using synthetic data, where large labeled datasets can be generated efficiently. However, strong performance on simulated data does not guarantee equally strong performance in experiments. Here, we benchmark five neural network architectures for quantum-dot state recognition using a shared synthetic training dataset and independent synthetic and experimental test sets. We compare convolutional and fully connected neural networks, a mixture density network, a vision transformer, and a U-Net across multiple training set sizes and two input normalization schemes. We find that model performance and rankings are closely preserved when moving from held-out synthetic patches to previously unseen simulated devices, but change substantially when the same models are evaluated on experimental data. In particular, the architecture achieving the highest synthetic performance is not the one that performs best experimentally. Input normalization further affects training behavior and, for some architectures, synthetic-to-experimental transfer. These results show that synthetic benchmark performance alone is insufficient to select models for experimental deployment and highlight the need to jointly evaluate architecture, preprocessing, data efficiency, model complexity, and experimental transfer when developing machine-learning tools for automated quantum-dot characterization and control.

items.title: Co layer Thickness Driven Structural Evolution and Magnetic Behaviour of Co/Ir/Co Trilayers
items.summary: Ferromagnetic heavy-metal (FM/HM) trilayer heterostructures provide a versatile platform for investigating the interplay between structural and magnetic properties. In this study, we investigate the effect of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of sputter-deposited $\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})/\mathrm{Ir}(5\,\mathrm{nm})/\mathrm{Co}(t_{\mathrm{Co}})$ varying from 2 to 10 nm. Structural characterization using grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) reveals a nanocrystalline structure, with the crystallite size increasing with Co-layer thickness. Furthermore, X-ray reflectivity (XRR) reveals a thickness-dependent variation in interface morphology, with the interface roughness ratio reaching a maximum at $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 4$ nm. Temperature-dependent zero-field-cooled and field-cooled (ZFC-FC) magnetization measurements reveal thickness-dependent characteristic temperatures and multiple relaxation regimes in selected samples, indicating complex thermally activated magnetic behaviour. In contrast, field-dependent hysteresis measurements reveal that the saturation magnetization increases with Co-layer thickness, whereas the coercivity exhibits a pronounced non-monotonic variation, with enhanced values at intermediate thicknesses. Moreover, low-temperature hysteresis loops display thickness-dependent exchange-bias-like shifts, particularly for $t_{\mathrm{Co}} = 2$-$4$ nm. These findings highlight the strong influence of Co-layer thickness on the structural and magnetic properties of Co/Ir/Co trilayers.

items.title: Exact Magnetic Confinement of a Doped Hole by Kinetic Frustration
items.summary: We establish an exact mechanism of magnetic confinement driven purely by kinetic frustration. In a finite open sawtooth $U=\infty$ Hubbard chain of $L$ unit cells doped with one hole, the ground state at magnetization $M$ contains $M$ polarized triplet dimers surrounding a connected singlet region of length $\ell_{\rm s}=L-M$. A magnetic field selects $M$ and hence the confinement length. The hole forms a standing wave in the singlet region with exponential tails in the triplet background. Confinement requires neither disorder nor an exchange-generated string tension: destructive interference between direct and apex-mediated hopping makes the triplet bonds reflecting. At $t_2/t_1=[2+4\cos(π/(\ell_{\rm s}+2))]^{-1/2}$, they become perfectly reflecting, producing a position-degenerate compact localized state. At every fixed field $0<h<h_{\rm sat}$, the singlet region remains finite as $L\to\infty$ and shrinks stepwise with increasing field, whereas at $h=0$ it spans the system.

items.title: First-order magnetostructural transition in Ni-Mn-Sn powder - A matter of particle and grain size
items.summary: In Ni-Mn-based Heusler alloys, the magnetocaloric effect originates from a first-order magnetostructural transition (FOMST). However, the influence of particle and grain size on thermal hysteresis, transition width, and nucleation and growth mechanism remains poorly understood, as mechanical grinding can introduce residual stresses and processing-induced defects. In this study, we examined the size dependence of the FOMST in gas-atomized Ni-Mn-Sn powder by combining microstructural characterization with temperature-dependent XRD, magnetometry, calorimetry and single-particle measurements, enabling decoupling of size dependence from processing-related influences. We observed a pronounced size dependence of the transition ranges (Ms-Mf) and (Af-As), which decrease with decreasing particle size and approach zero for single-crystalline particles below ~20-30 micrometer. The thermal hysteresis decreases with increasing particle size, reaching a lower limit of 17 K for large polycrystalline particles above 100 micrometer. EBSD reveals a nearly constant grain size, implying a transition from polycrystalline to single-crystalline particles as particle size decreases. In polycrystalline particles, multiple grains transform gradually over an extended temperature interval because grain boundaries act as barriers to the progression of transformation. In contrast, single-grain particles lack preferred nucleation sites, resulting in larger hysteresis, while the absence of barriers to transformation propagation causes the entire particle to transform in a narrow range. These results demonstrate that the size dependence of the FOMST is governed by the interplay between particle size, grain boundaries, and the free particle surface.

items.title: Effect of Size Asymmetry and Zwitterionic Character of Solvent Ions on Impedance Spectra of Ultradilute Colloidal Suspensions
items.summary: Buffer chemistry modulates colloidal impedance critically for label-free biosensing and electrokinetic diagnostics, yet classical models neglect buffer-specific interactions. We studied carboxylated polystyrene (PS) microspheres in conductivity-matched zwitterionic 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-piperazineethanesulfonic acid (HEPES) and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). Two concentration-dependent regimes emerged: oscillatory at ultradilute concentrations (<0.02 w/v%; Region 1) and monotonic at higher concentrations (Region 2). In Region 1, HEPES at pH 6.9 (approximately 80% zwitterionic) produced the largest deviation of delta Z from the O'Brien prediction. The conductivity increment was opposite in sign to classical expectation. We attribute this to zwitterion-driven interfacial ordering that enhances local conductivity and promotes self-limiting particle clustering. Dynamic light scattering detected cluster formation at 0.008 w/v%, well below aggregation thresholds. Changing pH from 6.9 to 8.1 strongly altered impedance amplitude; DLS profiles remained invariant. This indicates zwitterions modulate electrochemical polarization, not physical assembly. Molecular dynamics simulations showed pH-dependent HEPES organization at the PS surface. At pH 6.9, interfacial charge- and number-density profiles showed comparable oscillatory periodicity. At pH 8.1, anionic HEPES produced a more diffuse profile with increased Na+ compensation. These results support interfacial ordering as a contributor to enhanced conductivity but do not establish discrete layers or registry. Zeta potentials distinguished stable HEPES interfaces from PBS, where magnitude increased with ionic strength, contrary to classical screening theory. These nonlinear signatures and mesoscale organization underscore the role of buffer selection in high-sensitivity impedance biosensing.

items.title: Phonon-Dressed Quasiparticles in Epitaxial Scandium Nitride Resolved by Soft X-ray ARPES
items.summary: Electron-phonon interactions govern quasiparticle energies, lifetimes, and temperature-dependent band structures in semiconductors. However, direct momentum-resolved experimental evidence of their impact on quasiparticle electronic structure remains scarce, particularly in nitride semiconductors. Here, we present conclusive experimental evidence of electron-phonon interaction-induced quasiparticle renormalization and pronounced spectral broadening in p-type scandium nitride (ScN), using soft x-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. First-principles spectral-function calculations due to electron-phonon coupling reproduce the measured spectra, capturing a pronounced quasiparticle kink ~2.3 eV below the valence-band maximum, phonon satellite features arising from long-range electron-phonon coupling, and a direct bandgap zero-point renormalization of -124.3 meV within the non-adiabatic Allen-Heine-Cardona approach. We further show that the anomalous temperature-induced increase in the direct bandgap in ScN originates from the combined effects of thermal expansion and electron-phonon coupling, contributing comparably near room temperature. Our results establish ScN as a model platform for visualizing electron-phonon coupling and provide a quantitative benchmark for predictive first-principles descriptions of quasiparticle renormalization in semiconductors.

items.title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
items.summary: We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of $s$ particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed $s$, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics. We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

items.title: Large spin large deviations for interacting particle systems
items.summary: We propose a novel framework for analyzing the sample-path large deviations of interacting particle systems directly on a lattice by considering a large-spin limit ($s \to \infty$). Through an appropriate scaling of variables, the process concentrates around its deterministic trajectory, governed by the lattice diffusion equation. We quantify the exponential cost of observing atypical trajectories by explicitly computing the path-space large deviation rate function from the scaled microscopic generator, based on a theory due to Feng and Kurtz. The rate function is described in terms of a Hamiltonian on a lattice in terms of classical spin variables. Notably, for our main model, the symmetric harmonic process, the corresponding Hamiltonian is identified with the classical integrable non-compact Ishimori spin chain. Furthermore, we show that our large spin large deviation theory is fully consistent with traditional Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT), smoothly recovering the standard MFT Hamiltonian in the spatial continuous limit. We also perform a Poisson-noise Martin--Siggia--Rose (MSR) computation to derive the non-linear lattice Hamiltonian directly from microscopic dynamics, use a relative entropy argument to obtain the density-current action, and establish the lattice fluctuation theorem alongside its symmetry origin. Overall, our framework provides a naturally regularized, lattice analogue of MFT that circumvents spatial ultraviolet singularities and possible continuous density blow-ups. We also apply our new scheme to partial symmetric exclusion process, symmetric inclusion processes, Brownian energy process and integrable heat conduction model, showing how their large-deviation Hamiltonians relate to classical compact and non-compact spin chains.

items.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
items.summary: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-particle exhibiting $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(2,N)}$ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-membrane possesses $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(3,N)}$ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of $(5{+}1)$D 1-form $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to $\mathbb{Z}_{2} \times \mathbb{Z}_{3}$, with the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ sector consistently captured by this process.

items.title: Spin-hydrodynamics in graphene and thermovortical magnetization
items.summary: We examine the framework of relativistic spin hydrodynamics in the context of the Dirac quasiparticle fluid in graphene. We develop a spin-hydrodynamic model for a (2+1)-dimensional system of fermions under the condition of small spin polarization. Our analysis confirms that thermal vorticity, which satisfies the global equilibrium condition, is also a solution to the spin-hydrodynamic equations. Additionally, we calculate the magnetization of the system in global equilibrium and introduce a novel phenomenon - thermovortical magnetization - resulting from thermal vorticity, which can be experimentally observed in graphene.

items.title: Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
items.summary: The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. Hydrogen binds cooperatively to the silicon vacancy, which goes directly from bare to fully passivated $V$H$_4$. In contact with water the bare vacancy is never the lowest-energy state. Near neutral pH it binds oxygen from water as the A center, the paramagnetic hydroxyl complex forms below about pH 5 at zero bias, and full passivation to $V$H$_4$ requires cathodic bias. In PBE the Fermi level barely moves these boundaries, because the acceptor levels lie at or above the conduction-band edge. In SiC the first hydrogen binds to the silicon vacancy by 1.97 eV but is unbound at the carbon vacancy (the $Z_{1/2}$ center), so hydrogen from water alone should not passivate it except under cathodic bias.

items.title: Diffusion of chiral active Brownian particles in oscillatory Poiseuille flow
items.summary: Micro- and nanoswimmers diffusing in a fluid flow confined to microchannels are often described by overdamped active Brownian particle dynamics, in which viscous effects dominate and inertia is negligible. Here, we investigate the diffusive behavior of chiral self-propelled particles in a two-dimensional microchannel with oscillatory Poiseuille flow. Using numerical simulations, we show that the effective diffusion coefficient strongly depends on the oscillation frequency, flow strength, intrinsic angular velocity, and rotational diffusion rate. Interestingly, the effective diffusion coefficient can oscillate with oscillation frequency and flow strength, exhibiting distinct maxima and minima. The enhanced diffusion peaks arise from resonant diffusion associated with the matching between the flow oscillation time scale and the intrinsic characteristic diffusion time scale. Moreover, we identify an additional vorticity matching mechanism, leading to alternating channel wall accumulation of particles during successive flow half-cycles. Additionally, chiral particles strongly amplify the resonant diffusion, producing diffusion enhancements of several orders of magnitude compared to nonchiral particles. The results of this study could have implications for controlling the diffusion of self-propelled particles in microfluidic channels using time-dependent flow.

items.title: Chemical Substitution as a Route to Anomalous Surface Superconductivity in NiBi$_3$
items.summary: Stabilizing two-dimensional superconductivity in a bulk superconducting material provides a unique route to exploring the interplay between superconducting condensates of different dimensionalities. Here, we present evidence for a distinct surface-associated superconducting state in Pb-substituted NiBi$_3$. NiBi$_{2.8}$Pb$_{0.2}$ exhibits a resistive onset at $T_{c,\mathrm{onset}}^{*}\approx8.1$~K, nearly twice the bulk superconducting transition temperature of approximately 4.1~K. The absence of a corresponding Meissner response or specific-heat anomaly at the higher-temperature transition supports its non-bulk origin. A cusp-like angular dependence of the critical field, well described by the two-dimensional Tinkham model, together with nonlinear current--voltage characteristics and signatures of a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless transition, establishes the low-dimensional character of this superconducting state. Remarkably, the surface-associated superconductivity persists well beyond the bulk upper critical field, reaching a maximum ratio of $H_{c3}/H_{c2}\approx4.3$, far exceeding the conventional Saint-James--de Gennes value of 1.695. These results demonstrate that Pb substitution can stabilize an anomalously enhanced low-dimensional superconducting state in NiBi$_3$, providing a platform for investigating superconductivity at the boundary of a bulk superconductor.

items.title: First-Principles Investigation of the Structural, Electronic, Optical, Elastic, and Thermoelectric Properties of X2MoSeO6 (X = K, Rb, Cs)
items.summary: Understanding how alkali-metal substitution influences the coupled physical properties of molybdenum selenite oxides is essential for establishing their composition-structure-property relationships. Although the lighter members of the X2MoSeO6 family have been investigated, the heavier alkali-metal compounds remain comparatively unexplored, particularly regarding their integrated electronic, mechanical, optical, and thermoelectric responses. Here, a comprehensive first-principles investigation of X2MoSeO6 (X = K, Rb, and Cs) is presented using density functional theory and semi-classical Boltzmann transport calculations. The optimized structures exhibit progressive unit-cell expansion with increasing alkali-metal ionic size, while their indirect electronic bandgaps vary non-monotonically, reaching 2.646, 2.216, and 2.427 eV for K2MoSeO6, Rb2MoSeO6, and Cs2MoSeO6, respectively. All three structures satisfy the elastic stability criteria, with Hill-averaged bulk moduli increasing from 16.332 to 20.975 GPa across the series. K2MoSeO6 exhibits the strongest elastic anisotropy, whereas Rb2MoSeO6 possesses the highest static electronic dielectric constant (4.614) and maximum absorption coefficient (2.291*106 cm-1). Thermoelectric calculations reveal pronounced carrier-polarity-dependent behavior, with Rb2MoSeO6 attaining a positive Seebeck coefficient of 390.55e-6 V/K at 100 K and an electronic-only figure of merit (ZTe) of 7.286 at 300 K under the selected positive-Seebeck condition. By extending the investigation to the K-Rb-Cs series, this work establishes a comparative foundation for understanding and further exploring the functional characteristics of molybdenum selenite oxides.

items.title: Dynamic Pseudogap Model: Analytic Results vs Monte Carlo Numerics
items.summary: Recently proposed dynamic pseudogap model analytical results for spectral density of an electron scattered by random time-dependent Gaussian field representing fluctuations with finite nesting vector ${\bf Q}$, characteristic oscillation frequency $ω_0$ and damping $γ$, leading to pseudogap formation, are compared with exact numerical solution by Monte Carlo (MC) approach. We consider both commensurate (real) and incommensurate (complex) fluctuations, for a wide range of parameters of the model. Electron Green's function is approximated either by a double Poisson series with history-dependent Bogoliubov gaps or by exact static continued fraction solution. In the coherent regime double-series representation provides description of dynamic sideband formation in the spectral density. As coherence is progressively lost, the theory crosses over to the quasistatic fluctuating-gap regime described by the exact continued-fraction solution. The exact MC solution overcomes the limitations of analytic approach, such as neglect of Magnus-type corrections in commuting approximation, and establish the limits of analytic approach, as well as confirming the exactness of continued fraction solution in static limit. In general, analytic expressions demonstrate rather satisfactory agreement with exact MC numerics within their limits, confirming the overall qualitative physical picture of dynamic pseudogap formation.

items.title: Random spin-3/2 antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains revisited
items.summary: We revisit the spin-reduction transition in the random spin-$3/2$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chain using the tensor-network strong-disorder renormalization group (tSDRG). The predicted transition separates two random-singlet (RS) phases: one formed by effective spin-$1/2$ moments at weaker disorder and the other by full spin-$3/2$ moments at stronger disorder. Within the Damle--Huse classification, this transition corresponds to an emergent permutation-symmetric $P_4$ multicritical point on a $P_2$ critical line associated with the RS phases. We first derive the critical exponents governing the disorder-averaged bulk and end-to-end correlation functions in the $P_n$ universality classes within the Damle--Huse framework. Using these theoretical predictions, together with a diagnostic constructed from the mean and variance of the energy-gap distribution, we identify the $P_4$ transition point and the reentrant behavior of the RS phase.

items.title: Electric-field controlled nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect in two-dimensional time-reversal symmetric systems
items.summary: It's established that the nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect (NANE), originating from Berry curvature near the Fermi energy, is symmetry-permitted only when the crystal symmetry in the transport plane of two-dimensional (2D) materials does not exceed a single mirror line. Here, we show that an applied direct electric field can lift this symmetry constraint, enabling an electric-field-induced NANE emerge in time-reversal symmetric 2D systems with higher crystallographic symmetries. This electric-field-induced NANE originates from two contributions: the Berry connection polarization, which roots in the electric-field-corrected Berry curvature, and the anomalous-velocity-modified nonequilibrium Fermi distribution function. Additionally, we propose an alternating temperature gradient as a driving force instead of the conventional steady one, ensuring experimental detection of NANE via second-harmonic measurement techniques. The behaviour of electric-field-induced NANE in the monolayer graphene has been theoretically and systematically investigated.

items.title: Holographic Timelike c-function
items.summary: The integration of high-energy degrees of freedom along the renormalization group (RG) flow in Poincaré-invariant theories is captured by a monotonic c-function. For such theories, holographic c-functions have been constructed using entanglement entropy. However, in theories with broken Lorentz invariance, these constructions generally fail, reflecting both the violation of entanglement RG monotonicity and its limitations in capturing essential features of nonrelativistic RG flows. Since many quantum many-body systems lack Lorentz invariance, it is important to identify a quantity that captures the decrease of effective degrees of freedom along such flows. We show that the recently introduced holographic timelike entanglement entropy naturally gives rise to a new c-function applicable to all such theories, which moreover obeys a geometric upper bound on its rate of change. We further demonstrate the existence of this c-function in theories with Lifshitz and hyperscaling-violating fixed points, showing that, provided the null energy condition, thermodynamic stability and explicit geometric conditions on the flow are satisfied, it obeys the expected RG monotonicity.

items.title: Why Fe doping kills photoluminescence in CsPbCl$_3$ but not in CsPbBr$_3$: Role of midgap Fe 3$d$ states and electron-phonon coupling
items.summary: Understanding the impact of transition-metal doping on the optoelectronic properties of halide perovskite nanocrystals is essential for their rational design in photonic applications. We establish the microscopic origin of photoluminescence (PL) quenching in Fe-doped CsPbCl$_3$ using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. The emergence of Fe 3$d$ midgap states creates efficient electron-trapping centres that drive nonradiative recombination, accounting for the reduced PL intensity. Extending this analysis to Fe-doped CsPbX$_3$ (X = Cl, Br), we show experimentally that although PL intensity is suppressed in both systems relative to their pristine counterparts, their high-doping behaviour diverges: CsPbCl$_3$ becomes completely non-emissive, whereas CsPbBr$_3$ retains a finite, saturated PL intensity. Despite this contrast, electronic structure calculations reveal nearly identical midgap states in both materials, indicating that electronic effects alone cannot explain the distinct PL responses. Phonon calculations likewise fail to capture this difference. In contrast, electron-phonon coupling calculations based on the deformation potential approach reveal significantly stronger coupling in Fe-doped CsPbCl$_3$, enabling efficient dissipation of electronic excitation energy into lattice vibrations and leading to complete PL quenching. These results identify electron-phonon coupling as the key factor governing halide-dependent PL quenching and provide a unified microscopic framework for dopant-induced nonradiative processes in halide perovskites.

items.title: Timelike Entanglement Entropy and Renormalization Group Flow Irreversibility
items.summary: We study holographic $c$-theorems based on timelike entanglement entropy and show that timelike $c$-functions capture irreversible renormalization group (RG) flow. We demonstrate that timelike $c$-functions are applicable to both relativistic and nonrelativistic quantum matter in nematic phases with broken rotational symmetry, and that they remain monotonic along holographic anisotropic RG flows under explicit geometric conditions, thereby passing some of the most stringent consistency tests. We derive the exact flow of the composite timelike $c$-function in general homogeneous anisotropic geometries and establish the $c$-theorem for adiabatic flows. Across all classes of scaling backgrounds examined, consistent with the null energy condition and thermodynamic stability, the monotonicity condition universally reduces to a constraint on a running geometric effective dimension. We further construct a second $c$-function purely from the imaginary part of the timelike entanglement entropy and prove its monotonicity under the local effective-dimension condition, without requiring adiabaticity. For Poincaré-invariant flows, this condition follows directly from the null energy condition. Moreover, we identify a geometric upper bound on the rate of change of the timelike $c$-functions, which constrains how rapidly effective degrees of freedom can be coarse-grained. Our results suggest that capturing RG irreversibility in nonrelativistic flows requires observables that are intrinsically sensitive to the temporal direction. The applicability of holographic $c$-theorems is thus extended to highly nontrivial RG flows and points toward a new information-theoretic diagnostic of holographic RG dynamics.

items.title: Unveiling Topological Fusion in Quantum Hall Systems from Microscopic Principles
items.summary: Establishing the fusion rules of anyonic quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall fluids is essential for understanding their underlying topological order. Building on the conjecture that key topological properties are encoded in the ''DNA'' of candidate many-body wave functions - that is, the pattern of dominant orbital occupations restricted to a finite number of lowest Landau levels - we propose a combinatorial framework that derives these fusion rules directly from microscopic data. By extending Schrieffer's counting argument and introducing classes of topological excitations, our framework provides a unified route to the fusion rules for both Abelian and non-Abelian excitations. This approach elucidates the emergence of topological features from first principles in both fermionic and bosonic systems. In particular, we unveil the previously unknown fusion rules of the Hafnian fluid.

items.title: Zeptojoule Microwave Calorimetry with Nanosecond Recovery in Graphene
items.summary: Graphene calorimeters are predicted to combine extreme energy sensitivity with rapid thermal recovery, yet experiments remain far from ideal estimates. Here, we directly calibrate a graphene Josephson-junction microwave calorimeter using nanosecond pulses and independently determine the thermal parameters of the same operating device. At 110 mK, calibrated pulse measurements yield a characteristic switching-energy scale of 18.1 meV (2.90 zJ), while time-resolved two-pulse thermometry gives an intrinsic relaxation time of 19.5 ns. Pulse-width-dependent calorimetry and bolometric thermometry show that the electronic heat capacity is 12.4 times and the electron-phonon coupling is approximately 50 times larger than ideal estimates. A thermal model using these measured parameters predicts 21.2 meV, quantitatively reproducing the observed switching response. These results identify the microscopic origin of the sensitivity gap in graphene calorimeters and establish a self-consistent calibration framework for ultrafast nanoscale thermal detectors.

items.title: Dephasing-powered open quantum-dot battery
items.summary: We propose a simple realization of an open quantum battery powered by local dephasing. The setup consists of a triple-quantum-dot chain coupled at one end to a thermal reservoir, with the dot at the opposite end strongly detuned to form a high-energy storage element. Local dephasing populates this highly excited state and autonomously drives the system into a nonequilibrium steady state with high ergotropic efficiency. We find a limit where the ergotropic efficiency approaches unity, while the ergotropy itself approaches one-third of the energy detuning. We characterize the battery through its energy-storage performance, charging time, and stability, showing that the charged state remains long-lived after the dephasing source is switched off. We then demonstrate two complementary protocols for extracting the stored energy. First, nearly all the available ergotropy can be recovered through a simple cyclic unitary protocol involving only modulation of the detuned-dot gate. Second, coupling the detuned dot to an electronic load allows the extraction of electrochemical work exceeding the initial ergotropy, thereby accessing part of the battery's passive energy. Our results establish local dephasing as an autonomous resource for charging open quantum batteries and demonstrate simple routes for extracting the resulting stored energy in experimentally accessible mesoscopic platforms.

items.title: Correlating Delayed Emission, Blinking Mechanism, and the Quantum-Confined Stark Effect in Single Quantum Dots
authors: Jialu Li, Xue Han, Changgang Yang, Mi Zhang, Zhihao Chen, Chuang Wang, Zhuang Ying, Jinhui Wang, Ruiyun Chen, Chengbing Qin, Jianyong Hu, Zhichun Yang, Jie Ma, Guofeng Zhang, Liantuan Xiao, and Suotang Jia
items.summary: Abstract Delayed emission, a long-lived nonexponential photoluminescence tail, is widely observed in quantum dots (QDs), but its microscopic origin and relationship with blinking and the quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) remain unclear. Here, we combine single-QD spectroscopy, time-gated photon analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations across CsPbX 3 perovskite, CdSe-based, and InP-based QDs to identify a potential mechanism. Delayed emission correlates with band-edge carrier-trapping blinking, but is weak in QDs dominated by trion-mediated Auger blinking, suggesting delayed emission is not universally tied to charge-separated states. Delayed photons originate from nanosecond-scale carrier trapping and detrapping at nonradiative recombination centers: transiently trapped carriers return to the band edge and recombine radiatively. Time-gated analysis distinguishes this process from QCSE-driven intensity-lifetime fluctuations on slower blinking time scales. Furthermore, we demonstrate that delayed photons compromise the single-photon purity at a fixed excitation repetition rate. These findings establish a general framework of delayed emission in QDs.

items.title: Mapping bimodal colloidal depletion systems onto the monodisperse gelation phase diagram
items.summary: Many industries rely on models of colloidal gelation and phase behavior to predict how processing equipment will handle new product formulations. In colloidal systems with nearly uniform particle size it is possible to predict the formation of a gel from only three state variables; however, the extension of this model to bimodal and multimodal systems is not well described. Here we present a systematic simulation study of the attractive bimodal depletion gel phase diagram. For these systems, we find that gelation is highly dependent on total volume fraction, attraction conditions, and bimodal composition. Attraction and composition can be effectively collapsed into a single parameter using the contact-weighted second virial coefficient. This successfully projects the bimodal phase diagram onto the established monodisperse phase diagram, including accurately describing most bulk assembly properties; however, the underlying network structure of these gels remains highly dependent on the details of bimodal composition and attraction.

items.title: Controlling transport with structured long-range hopping
items.summary: The combined effects of disorder and long-range hopping play an important role in determining localization and transport in low-dimensional quantum systems. We study transport in a one-dimensional disordered chain with nearest-neighbor hopping supplemented by a long-range hopping term. The long-range coupling is characterized by site-dependent amplitudes that may be either uniform or random. We investigate the interplay between diagonal disorder and long-range hopping, characterizing the resulting transport efficiency. We find that nearest-neighbor hopping in the presence of uniform long-range hopping amplitudes strongly suppresses delocalization over a range of weak disorder. The disorder-enhanced transport regime, established in previous studies, can be understood here as the recovery of delocalization from this strongly suppressed regime. An analytical solution in the Anderson eigenstate basis reveals the microscopic origin of this behavior. In particular, we show that the low-disorder regime of strongly suppressed delocalization can be eliminated by introducing randomness into the long-range hopping amplitudes, providing an additional mechanism for enhancing transport and qualitatively changing the response of the system to disorder.

items.title: Distributional statistics of nonequilibrium
items.summary: We establish a reference modeling framework for random probability distributions subject to constraints. Generalizing the hyperensemble approach of Crooks, we formulate Jaynesian priors of maximal uncertainty over the unit simplex of categorical distributions. This framework is entirely general, but we primarily investigate models with constraints on physically relevant quantities, namely, average energy and Shannon entropy. A constraint on the exact value of average energy uniquely determines a Boltzmann-Gibbs equilibrium, but also defines a hyperplanar subset of the probability simplex consisting of all distributions with that value of average energy. The associated hyperensemble has a uniform probability density across all such distributions, regardless of distance to equilibrium. Such reference models make predictions of generic nonequilibrium properties such as the mean and modal microstate distributions and the expected free energy of a random distribution, which we examine analytically and via exact sampling algorithms. Moreover, introducing constraints on Shannon entropy permits parametric access to tunably nonequilibrium regimes. The approach follows conventional Jaynesian modeling logic and is compatible with standard Bayesian inference, and reduces to Boltzmann-Gibbs statistics when Shannon entropy is maximized. We examine the physical predictions of this scheme, and demonstrate its wide compatibility with other approaches to nonequilibrium modeling. We illustrate the framework in three scenarios: (i) comparison to superstatistics quasi-equilibrium modeling, (ii) generation of random nonequilibrium steady states, and (iii) Bayesian inference under a prior hyperensemble. We highlight numerous prospects for theoretical extensions and empirical application.

items.title: Eutectic and peritectic equilibria in coherent binary alloys
items.summary: This work extends the Cahn--Larché thermodynamic framework to binary alloys in which two coherent solid phases coexist with an incoherent liquid and investigates how coherency strain energy modifies classical eutectic and peritectic equilibria. We derive equilibrium conditions for three-phase coexistence that include an elastic energy term dependent on the molar fractions of the solid phases and apply them to model binary eutectic and peritectic systems. We find that coherency stress transforms the eutectic point into a finite three-phase equilibrium field spanning a continuous range of compositions and temperatures. In systems whose equilibrium compositions are peritectically ordered, coherency stress progressively destabilizes the two-solid equilibrium without generating a stable three-phase field and can suppress the peritectic reaction entirely. This asymmetry is governed by the geometric relationship between the compositions of the phases: when the liquid composition lies between those of the two solids (eutectic configuration), the liquid serves as a thermodynamic buffer against the coherency penalty on the solid--solid pair; when it lies outside (peritectic configuration), no such mechanism is available. These results demonstrate that coherency stress can fundamentally alter three-phase equilibria involving a liquid and suggest that such effects may be significant in systems with large coherent misfits.

items.title: Membrane-induced eggshell biomineralization towards controllable crystallization
items.summary: Abstract The avian eggshell is an extreme example of rapid biomineralization, yet how its underlying substrate, the eggshell membrane (ESM), initiates this process remains elusive, and the application potential of this fundamental biological mechanism has yet to be explored. Across the 33 avian species examined, ESMs consistently promoted CaCO 3 crystallization under standardized in vitro conditions and exhibited low heterogeneous nucleation barriers. Inspired by this mechanism, we designed a biomimetic fibrous membrane (b-FM) that reproduces the structural and chemical features of natural ESMs. The b-FM achieves a deposition rate of 0.58 mg cm −2 day −1 , surpassing the fastest natural ESM (0.46 mg cm −2 day −1 ). This efficiency arises from a threefold synergistic mechanism: (1) strong negative surface potential promoting Ca 2 ⁺ accumulation, (2) reduced heterogeneous nucleation energy barrier, and (3) regulated crystallization pathways. Demonstrating its application potential, a b-FM/glass fiber mesh (b-FM/GF) composite module was employed for water softening in a circulating cooling-water system. In a 30-day continuous circulation experiment, the b-FM/GF-treated system maintained softened water quality and effectively suppressed pipe scaling, with less than 2% reduction in the effective pipe area. These findings reveal shared features of ESM-promoted mineralization and establish design principles for industrial crystallization control.

items.title: Programming fibre circuits during spinning
A neural accelerated surface-roughness-based Discrete Element Method (SR-DEM) for modeling granular systems
items.summary: The Discrete Element Method (DEM) is an indispensable tool for modeling and understanding the basic mechanical behaviors of (dry) granular media, a class of disordered material systems of significant interest to multiple scientific domains from (geo-)physics to (chemical) engineering. At the core of all present DEM frameworks is a phenomenological friction law--commonly chosen to be of the Amontons-Coulomb type--that models the frictional interaction among constituent grains. Here, inspired by research in the tribology community, we present an alternative, fundamentally different framework, termed surface-roughness-based DEM (SR-DEM), in which contact friction is handled in a more physics-based manner. In this framework, instead of using a friction law, we explicitly resolve the surface topography of each grain and let friction emerge from collective frictionless interactions of surface asperities. In essence, we trade phenomenology for physics at the cost of an increased computational demand. To mitigate the cost, we introduce an FE$^2$-like algorithm and a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM)-based neural network surrogate, both of which are parallelized on GPU to accelerate contact computation. Crucially, using this framework in 2D, we (1) demonstrate the possibility of recovering a two-body-based Amontons-Coulomb-type friction behavior using a simple representation of surface topography, and (2) identify many-body-based frictional behaviors--more specifically, the angle of repose values--that cannot always be captured by current DEM frameworks under the same level of model complexity. We conclude by discussing future directions for SR-DEM, as well as exciting new opportunities it could unlock for a wide range of emerging applications, including (designing) suspension rheology and metamaterial mechanics.

items.title: Toward catalyst-mediated growth of diamond and cubic boron nitride wires
items.summary: Sustained catalyst-mediated growth of diamond and cubic boron nitride (cBN) wires has yet to be established reproducibly, although related methods produce carbon and BN nanotubes and many elemental and compound nanowires. I hypothesize that a retained contact between a catalyst and an existing tetrahedral crystal can sustain wire extension under conditions that do not nucleate that crystal on an otherwise comparable unseeded catalyst. The prediction is repeated, vapor-derived target-phase extension during an interval in which matched unseeded contacts do not nucleate that phase. I develop tests using diamond seeds, SiC starter wires and cBN seeds, separating the conditions used to establish the contact from those used for continuation. Worked estimates distinguish bulk precipitation driving forces from sidewall costs and show why increased carbon activity alone cannot select diamond over graphite. Comparisons with established synthesis identify the roles of pressure, hydrogen and activated nitrogen that must be retained or replaced. Isotope tracing, local structural measurements and time-dependent growth distinguish continued incorporation from seed consumption, conversion and etching. Nanometer, micrometer and larger wires could provide electrically insulating thermal connections, mechanical probes and reinforcing filaments.

items.title: Real-Time FPGA-Based Multi-Parameter Feedback Stabilization of a Silicon Double Quantum Dot
items.summary: Long term operation of semiconductor spin qubits requires active stabilization of quantum dot potentials against low-frequency charge noise. To address this, we demonstrate a gradient-descent feedback approach in a silicon double quantum dot device using high-bandwidth radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry readout and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for digital signal processing. This architecture enables continuous multi-parameter gradient calculation and quick gate voltage updates, significantly increasing the effective feedback bandwidth compared to previous methods relying on slow direct-current transport measurements. By operating with 8 steps per feedback cycle and an integration time of 25.6 $μ$s, this high-speed stabilization scheme maintains better than -6 dB of noise suppression up to 5 kHz, achieving an attenuation of $-7.4 \pm 0.2$ dB at the maximum measured frequency. This effectively suppresses low-frequency 1/f noise, maintaining device stability over longer time periods, and potentially enables real-time control in large-scale quantum dot arrays.

items.title: Elasto-Plastocapillarity: Surface-Tension-Driven Flows of Yield-Stress Fluids
items.summary: In this perspective article, we introduce elasto-plastocapillarity: surface-tension-driven free-surface flows of yield-stress fluids in which capillary stresses compete with yielding and elastic relaxation. We frame the relevant parameter space, and highlight representative problems (drops, bubbles, jets/filaments, thin films, and porous media) that are central to applications ranging from additive manufacturing and coatings to biological flows. We then outline a set of timely open challenges, including surface-tension measurements, breakdown of scale separation near the microstructures, coupled bulk-interface flow experimental diagnosis, interfacial rheology and surface stresses, history dependence, constitutive models and boundary conditions, reduced theoretical models, and the emerging opportunity provided by artificial intelligence and microgravity; aimed at guiding future experiments, theory, and computation.

items.title: Fate of Quantum Scars and Chaos-Assisted Tunneling under Dissipation
items.summary: Quantum scars enable memory and recurrent dynamics, but their fate under dissipation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that distinct quantum scars can respond qualitatively differently to the same dissipative channel. We consider a collective spin model coupled to a lossy cavity and, guided by its classical limit, identify scars associated with two unstable structures: a saddle point on a dissipation-free invariant manifold with vanishing cavity field and an unstable superradiant fixed point with finite photon occupation. The former is immune to photon loss in the classical limit and exhibits persistent quantum revivals, whereas the latter couples directly to the dissipative channel, but exhibits slow dynamics. Remarkably, the superradiant scar also supports chaos-assisted quantum tunneling between two symmetry-related, macroscopically distinct semiclassical configurations, despite the presence of dissipation. Our results identify an experimentally accessible setting for exploring dissipative scarring and chaos-assisted tunneling in cavity QED.

items.title: OpenFerro: a unified framework for mesoscale ferroic dynamics and enhanced sampling
items.summary: Modeling ferroic materials requires connecting microscopic fluctuations to collective dynamics over mesoscales. We introduce OpenFerro, a unified lattice-field dynamics framework that combines flexible Hamiltonians, automatic differentiation, parallel execution, and enhanced sampling. The same framework can simulate ferroelectric domain motion, magnetic disordering, and coupled spin-lattice thermodynamics. On four graphics processors, a bulk BaTiO$_3$ benchmark with long-range dipolar interaction reaches $840^3$ unit cells, representing 3 billion atoms through the retained lattice variables. We simulate polarization textures in a PbTiO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ superlattice spanning $0.8~μ\mathrm{m}$ laterally and a BaTiO$_3$ nanoparticle 200~nm in diameter, retaining unit-cell resolution. We also demonstrate enhanced-sampling simulations that reconstruct the polarization free-energy surface of bulk BaTiO$_3$ without a prescribed polynomial form. With moderate computational resources, OpenFerro achieves atomistic-resolution simulations at mesoscopic scales traditionally studied with continuum models.

items.title: Ab initio calculations of $^{229}$Th band-to-band internal conversion rate in $^{229}$ThO$_2$
items.summary: We present an ab initio calculation of the band-to-band internal-conversion rate of the $\hbarω_{\rm nuc} \approx 8.35$ eV isomeric transition in $^{229}$ThO$_2$. Because the nuclear transition energy exceeds the electronic band gap of ThO$_2$, the isomer can decay nonradiatively by resonantly promoting a valence electron into the conduction band. We formulate this process as a Brillouin-zone sum over vertical interband transitions weighted by local Th-centered hyperfine matrix elements, which are evaluated directly from all-electron full-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave Bloch spinors. A finite nuclear magnetization model is included to regularize the short-range hyperfine interaction and to account for the Bohr-Weisskopf effect. After applying scissor shifts to span the experimentally reported ThO$_2$ band gaps, we find calculated internal-conversion lifetimes in the range of $1-16~μ{\rm s}$. The lifetime increases strongly as the band gap approaches $ω_{\rm nuc}$ because the resonant interband phase space at the nuclear transition energy is reduced. For the larger reported ThO$_2$ gaps, the calculated lifetime is comparable to the measured conversion-electron Mössbauer lifetime [Nature 648, 300 (2025)]. Our analysis implies that choosing solid-state hosts with band-gap values slightly lower than $ω_{\rm nuc}$ can optimize solid-state nuclear clock performance with internal-conversion electron readout.

items.title: Ubiquity of ocular resonances in scattering phenomena
items.summary: We demonstrate how quantum mechanical scattering off a potential with a characteristic surface generically leads to a family of resonances in the complex momentum plane clustered near a roughly eye-shaped curve centered on the origin and formed by anti-Stokes lines. A particularly interesting class are potentials that are more singular than $1/r^2$ at short distance, where the scattering surface is the separatrix between captured and deflected classical trajectories. These resonances have been recently shown to play an important role in low energy nucleon scattering, and can be related to ``creeping waves'' familiar from classical diffractive scattering and analyzed by means of Regge poles.

items.title: Optimal Search Strategies under Finite Resource Constraints
items.summary: Improving target search is a challenge faced by many natural and artificial agents, often requiring the use of energetic or material resources. These inputs may be supplied by an external controller or generated by the searcher itself, for example, through the deposition of cues along its trajectory. Although such resources are commonly modeled as costly but available without an explicit limit, in practice, they can often only be produced in finite amounts. Here, we go beyond the assumption of an unlimited supply of resources by investigating searches in which a finite resource budget must be allocated throughout the search process. To investigate this problem, we equip a one-dimensional diffusive searcher with three types of resources: an external force, a supply of partially reflecting flags, and auto-chemotactic cues. We derive exact optimal resource-allocation protocols for informed search processes in which the agent has continuous access to its past and current positions, which we find to always require resource allocation to be spatially concentrated. We then determine the corresponding protocols for blind searchers and show that resource usage must be more evenly distributed. Non-Markovian cues that generate environmental memory are found to substantially improve search performance when the agent has access to positional information, even under finite-resource constraints. In contrast, their benefits are considerably more limited for blind search, particularly when the cues provide no directional information.

items.title: Exploring Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures for Self-Supervised Representation Learning of Powder X-ray Diffraction Patterns
items.summary: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) is the primary high-throughput method for resolving crystal structures, a cornerstone of materials science. As high-throughput synthesis and self-driving laboratories advance, automated XRD pattern analysis has become vital for accelerating materials discovery. However, traditional matrix factorization methods fail when lattice variations cause non-linear peak shifts. At the same time, supervised learning approaches face a combinatorial explosion when handling multi-phase mixtures. To overcome these challenges, we adopt a self-supervised Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to learn representation embeddings from 1D diffraction patterns. By optimizing a masked self-prediction loss directly within the latent space, the framework captures high-level crystallographic semantics. Downstream evaluations show that lightweight attentive probes trained on frozen JEPA representations achieve space group classification and lattice parameter estimation accuracy close to much larger supervised vision transformers. Furthermore, latent probing reveals that the learned representation space naturally organizes physical transformations, isolating smooth trajectories for peak broadening. Interestingly, decoding along latent paths between single-phase crystal representations yields realistic multi-phase mixture patterns, demonstrating an emergent continuous structure learned without explicit multi-phase supervision.

items.title: Chern non-trivial two-dimensional square-net nodal line semimetal
items.summary: We investigate a two-dimensional $p_xp_y$ square-net tight-binding model with two sublattices and introduce a symmetry-informed, momentum-dependent spin-orbit coupling (SOC) with a finite-range real-space hopping representation. Its two components jointly gap the nodal line, while one breaks time-reversal symmetry, producing a Chern-insulating phase with an occupied band Chern number $C=2$. Nanoribbon calculations reveal edge-localized states traversing this gap, with two net chiral modes per edge. We further show that the conserved spin sectors are unitarily equivalent and therefore have equal Chern numbers, ruling out a nontrivial time-reversal-protected $\mathbb{Z}_2$ phase within this ansatz. Our results establish a phenomenological route to Chern topology in square-net two-dimensional systems and clarify the symmetry constraints governing the accessible insulating phases.

items.title: Autonomous atomistic-continuum coupling through uncertainty-aware active learning
items.summary: We develop an uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling approach for coupling an atomistic kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) surface-chemistry solver with a continuum multi-species fluid dynamics solver across disparate physical length and time scales. The surrogate model predicts boundary mass fluxes for six species and their uncertainties, which the continuum solver monitors to automatically trigger additional KMC simulations when new training data are needed. This enables efficient multiscale coupling and maintains a user-specified level of accuracy. We demonstrate the approach for reactive halide-perovskite vapor deposition, which involves a multi-species vapor jet impinging on a reactive substrate. The KMC solver uses a DFT-calibrated energetics model that we construct as part of this work and provides net deposition and desorption rates for six species. With a conservative uncertainty threshold, the surrogate-coupled approach reproduces cumulative mass fluxes of the directly coupled approach with errors typically within 10-20%, while capturing the non-monotonic dependence of net deposition on species partial pressure. Importantly, the results show that detailed crystal structure need not be explicitly represented to predict quantities exchanged between atomistic and continuum solvers; species-resolved mass fluxes provide a sufficiently low-dimensional representation of the atomistic response. For this accuracy target, the autonomous online-learning approach reduces the number of required atomistic simulations by two to three orders of magnitude relative to direct multiscale coupling.

items.title: Unified First-Principles Theory of Finite-Wave-Vector Photocurrents in Crystals
items.summary: Spatially structured light carries independent phase and envelope variations in addition to its polarization and frequency. We develop a first-principles theory of second-order dc photocurrents (especially shift and injection) that resolves how these optical degrees of freedom drive distinct dc responses in crystals. The second-order dc response couples two optical field components at the same frequency but with generally different wave vectors. Expanding the response to first order in these wave vectors identifies two rank-four material tensors: $ξ$, which couples to the optical phase gradient and contains the plane-wave photon-drag limit, and $ζ$, which couples to the intensity gradient and describes a spatially varying dc current. Wannier-interpolated calculations for monolayer GeS show symmetry-allowed finite-wave-vector responses that survive at a centrosymmetric structure where conventional bulk photovoltaic effect vanishes. For a Gaussian beam with a uniform phase gradient, the phase-gradient contribution drives current in the same direction on both sides of the beam center, whereas the intensity-gradient contribution drives currents in opposite directions, showing that distinct photocurrent patterns can be selected through the wavefront and envelope of light. A multipolar analysis further resolves the optical corrections into electric-quadrupole, orbital magnetic-dipole, and band-dispersion contributions. Together, these results show how the spatial structure of light can serve as an independent control variable for nonlinear photocurrent generation and provide a first-principles route to predict this response in real materials.

items.title: Precipitation-dissolution cycling drives intermittent salt creeping
items.summary: Salt creeping --- the precipitation of salt crystals away from an evaporating liquid interface along surrounding surfaces --- occurs across settings from geology and cultural-heritage weathering to inkjet printing and carbon sequestration. Yet why its dynamics are sometimes smooth and sometimes violently intermittent has remained unexplained. Here we investigate the confined evaporation of salt solutions from a capillary with unidirectional water loss, and show that intermittent salt creeping is driven by a cycle of precipitation and dissolution sustained entirely by liquid transport. Time-resolved measurements reveal that each burst of crystal growth coincides with episodic imbibition of solution into the growing salt deposit on the outer capillary surface, which couples evaporation to crystallization. Combining experiments with a minimal theoretical model, we show that the difference between the supersaturation at which crystals nucleate and the saturation concentration at which they redissolve --- the metastable zone of the salt --- is sufficient to generate this cycle. The same mechanism accounts for the cases in which creeping is not intermittent: where the concentration at the capillary exit never reaches the nucleation threshold the liquid meniscus recedes smoothly, and where it cannot subsequently fall back below saturation the deposit grows continuously, exhibiting self-amplified creeping. Our results recast salt creeping as a relaxation oscillator, and identify precipitation-dissolution cycling as a generic route to intermittency in evaporating multicomponent fluids.

items.title: Phase transitions through excited-state level crossings and topological indicators: the case of the XXZ chain with staggered Ising interaction
items.summary: We combine two ways of determining the phase diagram of the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain with a staggered Ising interaction and uniform transverse exchange, based on exact diagonalization. The model realizes a competition between Néel order and bond-dimerized phases generated by the alternating Ising interaction. The simplest approach to determine the phase boundaries is to use topological indicators based on generalized position operators (GPOs). We show that in general, the bosonized and numerical results for the topological indicators agree. The second is the method of crossings of excited energy levels (MCEL), which is justified by conformal field theory. Despite the partial loss of translational symmetry induced by the alternating Ising interaction, we show that, with the aid of the GPO to identify the relevant level crossings, the MCEL provides an accurate determination of the phase boundary between the Néel and dimerized phases. While the jumps of a topological indicator based on a GPO provide a qualitatively correct phase diagram, its accuracy is affected when the gap is very small (or the correlation length very large) at one side of the transition, as we show using field-theoretical arguments. The combination of both methods provides a more efficient way of calculating phase diagrams for correlated one-dimensional models than other widely used conventional approaches.

items.title: Winding-Controlled Topological Descendants of Antialtermagnets
items.summary: Odd-parity spin splitting constrains magnetic band crossings but does not determine their topological descendants. We show that the Chern contribution of an isolated inverted sector is controlled by the phase winding of its transverse mass pair: when the masses and tangential velocities reverse together, contributions from successive Dirac points add rather than cancel. This distinguishes topological winding from the polynomial degree labeling the magnetic parent. For specified complementary masses, periodic tetragonal $h$- and hexagonal $j$-wave models host eight and twelve same-chirality Weyl points on a momentum plane, with gapped-slice Chern numbers $|C|=4$ and $6$, respectively. A microscopic four-band $p$-wave model identifies an antiunitary obstruction to first-order transverse masses and demonstrates a symmetry-broken $C=1$ phase at quarter filling. First-principles calculations for the proposed coplanar spin-vortex texture of LaMnAu$_5$ reveal the $h$-wave nodal pattern, its anisotropic spin--orbit reconstruction, and a mirror-channel spectral response that reverses under opposite spin rotations. Together, these results distinguish the symmetry of an odd-parity magnetic parent from the mass structure controlling the topology of its descendants.

items.title: Evolution of microstructure and crystallographic texture in a novel Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy during hot rotary swaging
items.summary: A multi-step induction-assisted hot rotary swaging route was developed for the novel dual-phase Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy to investigate the evolution of microstructure, crystallographic texture, and mechanical properties during sequential deformation. Phase-transformation temperatures determined by electrical resistivity measurements were used to select processing conditions in the single-phase $β$ field at 880°C and the $α+β$ field at 780°C. Induction heating with thermographic temperature control enabled reduction of the initial 12 mm rod to 6.3 mm, corresponding to a total area reduction of 72%. Swaging in the $β$ field refined millimetre-sized prior-$β$ grains to approximately 100 $μ$m, while subsequent cooling produced a fine lamellar $α+β$ microstructure. Further deformation in the $α+β$ field disrupted the lamellar structure, promoted globularisation and recrystallisation of the $α$ phase, and refined the $β$ phase. The microstructural evolution was accompanied by a pronounced $\langle 11\bar{2}0\rangle_α\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ fibre texture in the $α$ phase, whereas the $β$ phase exhibited predominantly $\langle 110\rangle_β\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ together with a $\langle 111\rangle_β\parallel\mathrm{SD}$ component. The phase constitution remained comparatively stable, with approximately 12-15 wt.% retained $β$ throughout processing. Subsequent $α+β$ swaging decreased the compressive yield strength from 1103 to 839 MPa while increasing plastic deformability, with a maximum fracture strain of 32%. Radial hardness heterogeneity was progressively eliminated. These results demonstrate that induction-assisted rotary swaging in selected phase fields provides an effective route for tailoring microstructure, texture, and mechanical response in dual-phase zirconium alloys.

items.title: Turning angle analysis reveals hidden anisotropies in intracellular transport
items.summary: Molecular motion within living cells provides a window into the physical principles underlying intracellular organization and transport. Yet a fundamental limitation remains: measured trajectories are often short, noisy, and randomly oriented, rendering spatial anisotropies inaccessible to conventional analyses. We show that turning-angle statistics provide a robust approach for uncovering anisotropies in anomalous diffusion. Using a two-dimensional anisotropic fractional Brownian motion model with random orientations, we show theoretically and through simulations that turning-angle distributions preserve signatures of anisotropy. We apply this approach to single-particle tracking data, including quantum dots in the cytoplasm of HeLa cells and membrane proteins in hippocampal neurons. Turning angles reveal hidden anisotropies in the motion of quantum dots and Kv1.4 channels, and in specific dynamical states of glycoprotein CD4. These results establish turning-angle analysis as a powerful strategy for detecting organization in complex environments and reveal that anisotropic anomalous diffusion is an {often} overlooked feature of intracellular dynamics.

items.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
items.summary: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.

items.title: Orbital Hall response of spin-1 fermions with a curved central band
items.summary: We investigate the orbital Hall effect in a three-band system described by a low-energy Hamiltonian containing both linear and quadratic momentum-dependent contributions. The linear term lifts the degeneracy between the dispersive bands, providing a minimal setting to study orbital transport in a multiband system with a curved central band. Within a quantum kinetic approach, we derive the intrinsic orbital Hall response and analyze its microscopic origin in terms of interband coherence induced by an external electric field. We show that the orbital Hall conductivity arises from the interplay between the momentum-dependent orbital character of the eigenstates and transitions between different bands. The spin-1 structure provides a particularly transparent platform in which the contributions associated with different interband channels can be identified separately. We further show that the differential orbital Hall response provides a direct probe of the low-energy structure, exhibiting distinct scaling singularities associated with the linear and quadratic bands, respectively, while remaining independent of the ultraviolet cutoff. Our results establish a connection between the multiband quantum geometry of spin-1 fermions and their transverse orbital response, and provide a simple framework for investigating orbital transport beyond two-band models.

items.title: Cooperation of itinerant and localized physics in the magnetic phase diagram of 214 Ruddlesden-Popper iridates
items.summary: The $5d^5$ Ruddlesden-Popper iridates Sr$_2$IrO$_4$ and Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ have attracted considerable attention as spin-orbit entangled analogues of the cuprates, yet the origin of their antiferromagnetic insulating state, of Slater or of Mott-Heisenberg type, remains debated. We find that both materials sit in an intermediate regime in which itinerant and localized electrons cooperate in stabilizing the antiferromagnetic order, with Ba$_2$IrO$_4$ slightly more correlated than Sr$_2$IrO$_4$. We obtain this by computing, within dynamical mean-field theory, the interaction-temperature phase diagram of a realistic three-orbital $t_{2g}$ Hubbard model with spin-orbit coupling. Our study shows that neither the behavior of the gap across the Néel temperature nor the spin-polaron features of the spectral function unambiguously identify the cooperative regime, whereas the two-peak structure of the optical conductivity is reproduced only there and therefore constitutes a reliable fingerprint. By placing both compounds in a common phase diagram, our results reconcile seemingly contradictory experimental and theoretical reports, and provide a unified framework for future studies of the 214 iridates and of other spin-orbit coupled correlated materials.

items.title: The Thermodynamic Complexity of Circuits
items.summary: When any physical system executes a logically irreversible (non-injective) step of a computation, the excess heat released over the Landauer limit is an energetic cost that cannot be recovered. In modern computers this cost vastly dwarfs the Landauer cost. Modern stochastic thermodynamics refers to this cost as the ``entropy production'' and has derived fundamental lower bounds on its value. Here we introduce a thermodynamic model of circuits using heat functions and investigate its entropy production, deriving new results on the thermodynamic complexity of circuits. We first show that computing the optimal heat functions for gates in a given circuit (minimizing the entropy production) is PP-complete and multiplicative approximation of those heat functions is NP-hard, but additive approximation admits a polynomial-time randomized algorithm. We give tight bounds for entropy production for certain specific families of circuits (on uniformly distributed inputs): an $n$-ary AND tree of depth $O(\log n)$ requires $Ω(n)$ entropy production, while a serial chain achieves $O(1)$ in an idealized model, showing an energy-depth tradeoff. The Batcher odd-even mergesort network on $n$ bits has $Θ(n)$ entropy production, asymptotically less than its $Θ(n \log^2 n)$ gate count. On random permutations of distinct integers its entropy production is $Θ(n \log^2 n)$, asymptotically exceeding the Landauer cost of sorting; but preceding it with Leighton and Plaxton's almost-sorting network reduces the total heat released to $O(n \log n)$. Finally, we show how to sort $n$ values with zero circuit entropy production over any exchangeable input distribution. Our framework also yields streamlined proofs of known results in stochastic thermodynamics on mismatch cost and modularity cost.

items.title: Study of localization properties under subsystem periodic driving
items.summary: Periodic driving provides a powerful route for controlling localization and engineering effective Hamiltonians in quantum systems. A localized one-dimensional Aubry-André chain can be driven into a fully delocalized phase when the entire system is driven below a critical frequency. Here, we ask whether such delocalization can be achieved by driving only a part of the system. We address this question using a two-leg ladder comprising an Aubry-André chain coupled to a periodically driven clean tight-binding chain. Exact numerical calculations show that, starting from a localized static ladder, subsystem driving below a critical frequency cannot achieve complete delocalization. Instead, a mixed phase emerges, with localized and delocalized states coexisting and the fraction of delocalized states varying nonmonotonically with the driving frequency. This behavior can be understood using local effective Hamiltonians. Although these effective Hamiltonians are derived analytically in the high-frequency regime, they can nevertheless predict the localization transition occurring in the moderate-frequency regime. In fact, by quantifying the emergent nonlocality of the Floquet Hamiltonian, we show that these effective Hamiltonians provide a valid description up to a crossover frequency that is lower than the critical frequency associated with the localization transition. Our results demonstrate an alternative route to Floquet engineering, in which the transport properties of a quantum lattice system can be modified by driving only a subsystem.

items.title: Direct tests of conformal symmetry with Rydberg atoms: assessment and proposals
items.summary: We propose a direct test of conformal symmetry using Rydberg-atom arrays. By arranging the atoms on a circle and measuring equal-time two-point correlation functions, the characteristic functional form predicted by conformal field theory can be tested directly. We estimate the number of experimental snapshots required to resolve this behavior with sufficient statistical precision. We further optimize the time-dependent ramp profile of the Rabi frequency~$Ω$ and detuning~$Δ$ used to prepare the target critical state adiabatically. The optimized profile achieves higher fidelity over much shorter evolution times than those employed in previous experiments. Taken together, these results suggest that a direct experimental test of conformal symmetry is feasible with current Rydberg-atom technology.

items.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
items.summary: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects.
